## 2026-07-30 (hf) — THE GRADED LEDGER IS TWO BOOKS, AND MY OWN (gn) CHECK COULD NOT HAVE SHOWN OTHERWISE

- **A correction of my own conclusion, first.** `(gn)` found that two Railway services — `funding-carry` and `yield-harvester-shadow` — both publish `perps-funding-carry-lshadow`, scanned the paper ledger for duplicate `trade_id`s, found none, and concluded: *"The paper LEDGER is CLEAN (82 closes, zero duplicate trade_ids) so the go-live grade and the baseline are intact."* **That check cannot detect the thing it was used to rule out.** Two independent processes open at different moments, so their ids (`{coin}:{opened_ts}`) never collide. A duplicate-id scan is blind to duplicate WRITERS by construction. When you test whether a shared key did damage, pick a test that *could* find the damage.
- **The detector that works is structural.** A carry process keys `positions` by coin and enters only `if c not in positions`, so **one process cannot hold two positions in the same coin**. Measured across **all 28 books and 1,706 episodes** in the ledger, same-pair overlapping holds appear in exactly **two**:

  | book | overlaps >60s | deepest | verdict |
  |---|--:|--:|---|
  | `perps-funding-carry-lshadow` | 7 | **9.14h** on HYPE | **TWO WRITERS** |
  | `event-listing-sniper` (retired) | 9 | 48.01h | declared — `pair` does not encode the exchange across ~100 CEXes |

  Every other book reads **zero**, so the signal is specific rather than an artifact of how ledgers are written. Sub-60s "overlaps" are excluded as close-and-reopen inside one loop: on this book those sit at **0.3s** while the real ones are 2–9 **hours**.
- **A second, independent line.** That ledger reaches **10 concurrent open positions on 27 occasions** while the book's own `MAX_POSITIONS` was **8** until 30-Jul. Reported as corroboration only, never as the accusation — caps move and the ledger does not record which one was in force.
- **And the STATE key is shared too, which is the mechanism.** `funding_carry_bot` persists `positions` to `bot_state[bot_id]` and restores them at boot, so two processes on one `bot_id` are two writers of **one position map**: each clobbers the other every loop, and a restart can restore the other's positions — so a single logical position can be tracked, and closed, by both. Same two-writers-one-key hazard `(gn)` named for the summary row, on the key where it corrupts position tracking instead.
- **WHAT IT COSTS: `n` is not one book's independent trades, and `t` scales with sqrt(n)** — so the go-live frontrunner's significance was overstated for a reason entirely separate from `(hc)`'s era problem. Two independent defects, same book, same gate, same afternoon.
- **SHIPPED, and it is a control rather than a note.** `scripts/audit_ledger_integrity.py` reports every book (registered selftest; exits non-zero on a LIVING two-writer book), and `golive_readiness` now treats integrity as a **PRECONDITION**: a book with a same-pair overlap can never be `READY` and the reason is printed **first** in `fails`, because buried at position three behind `fails[:2]` it was invisible in exactly the run that needed it. It is deliberately **not** a seventh bar — `BAR_NAMES` is the published contract the dashboard renders — and it invalidates the other six rather than joining them. The 🚦 card grows a red `2 writers` chip. Published as `integrity` so no consumer string-matches prose.
- **ONE OWNER, and it is the consumer**: the three primitives live in `golive_readiness` (which ships inside the freqtrade image and does the grading) and the audit imports **them**. The reverse would drag a non-shipped script into the image's import graph — the born-dark class — and a second copy would let the audit and the gate disagree about the same ledger. `test_the_audit_and_the_gate_share_ONE_owner` asserts identity, not just equality.
- **OPERATOR ACTION, now more than cosmetic: one of the two services must be stopped in Railway.** A guard cannot un-pool closes two processes already wrote, and every grade over this window inherits it. CLAUDE.md's `(gn)` paragraph is struck through and corrected in place.

## 2026-07-30 (hd) — THE BRAIN WAS GRADING THE SAME BOOK ACROSS THE SAME BOUNDARY

- `bot_learn.ERA_START` exists for exactly this — its own header: *"Hypotheses must come from trades taken by the CURRENT code"* — and had **no entry for 🌾 `perps-funding-carry`**. So immediately after `(hc)` scoped the go-live gate to the book's post-17-Jul self, the brain was still grading the pre-fix and post-fix accrual bases **together**. Two organs, one ledger, two different histories.
- **This is the purest case the table describes, and it is not a strategy change.** It is an ACCOUNTING one: the `lighter_shadow` arm's accrual basis moved from per-hour to the venue's own per-8h settlement, and for a funding book `accrued` *is* the reported P&L and the win/loss call. Every pre-fix close is denominated in a unit the book no longer uses.
- **What it was actually holding up.** `brain-diagnosis` carries an **actuator-bearing** `regime_gate` on this book's `long` bucket (`seen: 69`) — and across the *whole* ledger the long side is only 13 closes, of which the positive evidence is **3 pre-fix `long_decay_paid` wins**. Scoped to the real era that bucket falls under the brain's n≥30 floor and the hypothesis correctly disappears. Fail-closed: an actuator resting on three pre-fix wins should not survive contact with the era it was taken in.
- **I checked before claiming and one of my two hypotheses was wrong.** I expected the brain to be *expanding* carry's stakes off inflated pre-fix wins (two-way mults since 21-Jul). It is not — `brain-stake-mults` currently publishes exactly **one** multiplier fleet-wide, `pm-abbott-lshadow|short-burst` reduce 0.75, and carry has none. So this change removes no existing expansion; what it does is stop one from ever being fabricated from pre-fix data. Stated because "the brain was over-sizing it" would have been a better story and was not true.
- The key `"perps-funding-carry"` also matches the RETIRED HL arm, harmlessly — it is in `LEGACY_BOTS` and the liveness filter drops it before any era lookup. Keyed **exactly**, not by substring: substring-matching this same pair is the `(gr)` near-miss that would have silently exempted the living twin.
- New cross-organ guard: where the gate's `POLICY_ERA` and the brain's `ERA_START` both declare a book they must **agree**. They may cover different sets — promotion eligibility and hypothesis generation are different questions — but a book cannot have two era-starts, or no reader can tell which history they are looking at. Brain selftest 51/51, suite green, five audits green.

## 2026-07-30 (hc) — 101% OF THE GO-LIVE FRONTRUNNER'S P&L PREDATES ITS OWN ACCOUNTING FIX

- **The gate that governs real money had no notion of when a book became itself.** `scripts/golive_readiness.py` graded every book on its **whole retained ledger**, so a change that made the earlier record *wrong* kept counting toward the 30-day bar. Measured on the book closest to real money — 🌾 `perps-funding-carry-lshadow`, the fleet's frontrunner at **five of six bars**:

  | opened | n | realised | mean/trade | t | bars |
  |---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
  | **before** 2026-07-17 | 25 | **+$62.03** | | | |
  | **since** 2026-07-17 | 57 | **−$0.91** | −0.005% | −0.08 | **2/6** |
  | pooled (what the gate read) | 82 | +$61.12 | +0.248% | **+2.60** | **5/6** |

- **101% of its entire realised P&L (+$62.03 of +$61.12) was opened before 17-Jul**, and it has been flat-to-negative for **13 days and 57 closes** since. Every number in the pooled row — the positive mean, the significant t, both halves positive — is carried by the earlier segment. What changed on 17-Jul is in the bot's own comment: the `lighter_shadow` arm's accrual line *"over-accrued 8x — straight into `accrued`, which IS this book's reported P&L and its win/loss call."* **For a funding book the accrual is the P&L.**
- **THE ERA DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REST ON THAT DIAGNOSIS.** A competing explanation is not eliminated: the venue's funding may simply have been hotter in early July (it is still hot — the live row shows carries at +84% to +722% APR), which shrinks accrual per hold with no bug at all. Either way the gate's own question — *does this book, as it now runs, make money* — is answered by the 57 closes, not the 25. **And the exact boundary is not load-bearing:** ≥17-Jul → 2/6, ≥22-Jul (n=28) → 2/6, ≥28-Jul (n=6) → 3/6. A finding that survives its own sensitivity analysis does not need the container archaeology settled — which matters, because the comment says 17-Jul while this file only entered `main`'s history on 28-Jul (PR #95).
- **SHIPPED: `POLICY_ERA`**, keyed BARE and suffix-stripped at lookup — the same table-keyed-bare / ledger-keyed-suffixed hazard the brain shipped for nine days (`bot_learn.era_epoch_for`, 23-Jul audit: *"every `ERA_START.get(bot)` missed and every bot was graded on its WHOLE retained ledger"*). Keyed on the **OPEN**, because a trade's policy is fixed when it is taken; a straddler accrued in **both** bases and belongs cleanly to neither. **Fail-CLOSED**: an unreadable open stamp is excluded when an era is declared, because counting a trade whose era cannot be determined is exactly the credit being withdrawn.
- **THE LIMIT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART.** An era resets on a change that makes earlier P&L *wrong* or the strategy *different in kind* — **not** on ordinary tuning. Carry's own 21-Jul `ENTER_APR` 0.40 → 1.60 is the worked example: real, deliberate, enacted from a sweep, and **not** an era reset even though splitting there would restrict the book *further* (n=31, −$0.76). The growth rail moves levers every day by design; a guard that reset the clock on each move would make the 30-day bar unreachable for every book forever, and `test_ordinary_tuning_is_NOT_an_era_reset` pins that.
- **NOTHING IS HIDDEN AND NOTHING IS PROMOTED.** Both samples publish — era-scoped is authoritative, `alltime` rides beside it — and the 🚦 card grows an `era 07-17` chip quoting both counts, with the all-time reading in its tooltip. `--min-closes` filters on the **all-time** count on purpose: an era'd book must show dark bars, never vanish, because vanishing reads as "never was a candidate". This is a REPORTING scope; `test_the_gate_still_promotes_nothing` asserts by AST that the file calls no actuator.
- **THE QUEUE REORDERS HONESTLY RATHER THAN EMPTYING.** With carry at 2/6, the fleet's actual frontrunner is now 💸 `perps-funding-lighter-lshadow` — n=85, 19.3d, mean +0.561%, t **+2.09**, failing only the 30-day window. The `(gk)` note had already spotted it at 5/6; it was simply standing behind a book whose case was pre-fix.
- 25 tests, mutation-verified two ways: keying the era on `close_ts` fails both the wiring test and the straddler count (`3 of 44`, not `4 of 44`); making `in_era` fail-open on a missing stamp fails the fail-closed parametrisation. Suite green (590), five audits green. Three of my own tests first failed on **page-wide substring scans** — `dry_run` and `era` both appear in the very sentences promising the properties being checked. Rewritten against AST and against the chip's own markup.

## 2026-07-30 (hb) — THE LIVE BOOKS WERE GRADED ON PRICES THEY NEVER OBSERVED

- **The one real-money finding that survived the refuter** (4 of 44 did). `_real_exit` returns `(px, measured, reason)` and falls back to the **DECISION price** on every failure path in `venues/fills.py` — a fallback its own docstring calls load-bearing. The repo's own measurements say that fallback is **universal**: *"0 of 81 live orders ever produced a measured fill"*, *"0 of 61 real orders ever id-matched"*. So `exit_price` on a live close row has been the price the bot **decided at**, never one it **observed** — and nothing on the row said so.
- **WHY THAT IS MORE THAN UNTIDY.** `scripts/golive_readiness.py` reads `fetch_paper_trades`. So do the brain and the promotion judge. **None of them can see a measured flag**, because `raw.measured` lives on `venue_orders` and no grading consumer joins that table. So the gate deciding whether a book may hold real money **could not distinguish a measured round trip from an assumed one** — against a gross edge the CHANGELOG puts at **+6.18bps/trade**, where the verdict turns entirely on round-trip cost.
- **SHARPER ON THE TAKER, and this is the part the auditor missed and the verifier caught**: `lighter_ticket_taker` sets `fee_rate = 0.0` for the LIVE arm on the stated premise that *"its spread is inside the real fill"* — **the exact premise `fills.py` measured false.** A live row can therefore carry zero fee AND zero spread.
- **SHIPPED: `exit_measured` / `exit_fill_src` on the close row of both live books.** Both closers already held the verdict as locals; the Farmer's blind-stop path was even **discarding it** with `_bpx, _, _ = _real_exit(...)` — the fail-safe that books a position it could not price, i.e. the last close whose basis should be a mystery. Now captured and stamped. Verified by AST: **3/3 Farmer sites and 2/2 Taker sites** carry provenance.
- **STRICTLY TELEMETRY, and the test proves it.** `fee_rate` is untouched, no bar, threshold or decision reads the new keys, and `test_no_exit_threshold_moved` pins every live exit constant at its known default. **Deciding what the fee should be has to start from how many closes were actually measured — which, until this row existed, was unknowable from the graded ledger.** Telemetry first, then the argument. Unknown is recorded as ABSENT rather than `False`, because a shadow arm has no venue fill and must not be logged as an unmeasured live one.
- **AND I NEARLY REPORTED A BUG I HAD NOT MADE.** My first test counted `measured=_meas` textually and read **5 occurrences for 3 call sites**, which looked exactly like a duplicate-keyword argument I had just injected into a real-money bot. I stopped and checked: three of the five are **pre-existing** `_slip_bps_of(..., measured=_meas)` calls. The patch was clean; **the count was the defect.** Rewritten to enumerate call sites by AST — a structural claim needs a structural check, which is the same lesson `(go)`'s text-proximity test taught six hours ago and I re-learned at a worse moment. (Also learned: `parametrize` over file CONTENTS builds a test id from the whole 4,000-line source, so one failure printed 240KB. Fixed with explicit ids.)
- Mutation-verified: dropping the stamp from ONE of the three Farmer sites fails exactly the site-coverage test. Suite green, three live selftests green, five audits green.

- **`(gt)` left one named blocker: the shipped rule was passed in BY HAND.** On pm-gillard a guessed `{tp 2%, sl 2%, 4h}` replayed to +0.030%/trade against a book whose real mean is negative, so the calibration gate correctly withheld everything.   * **UNITS** — Snap Back's exit is **40 bps** and the sniper's hold is in **seconds**; raw reads would be 4,000% and 21,600 hours.
  * **NOT AN ENV VAR AT ALL** — the sniper's TP/SL/hold are **bare module literals** (`TAKE_PROFIT_PCT = 0.15`). No env var, no lever: only a code edit and a redeploy can move them, so that book cannot participate in the growth rail however good a value is eventually found. Recorded in `HARDCODED_EXITS`.
- **EVERY BOOK'S REAL EXIT, now readable in one call.** Two are stark: **🌊 Tide Rider `{sl 35%}` and 📊 Index Rider `{sl 15%}` — one price exit each and NO TIME BOUND.** A position is held forever unless it loses 35%/15%. That is the zero-closes mechanism stated in the actual constants.
- **CALIBRATION PASSES.** With gillard's real rule (`tp 1%, sl 1%, 6h`, read via `parliament.strategies.base_params` — the same call the running bots make, so env overrides and clamping apply as in production): replayed **−0.158%/trade vs actual −0.110%**, gap 0.047pp against a 0.25pp tolerance, and **conservative in the right direction**. The replayed exit MIX independently matches `(gq)`'s ledger reading: `sl 133 / tp 95 / max_hold 11`. **The harness now reproduces the book, so its counterfactuals mean something.** First one in the fleet.
- **A REAL BUG IN MY OWN FLOOR, found by inspecting a refusal instead of trusting it.** The verdict said keep-shipped; I checked why and it was **not** the both-halves floor — that candidate passes both halves. It was refused on `peak_open` 6 vs 5, because I bounded exposure against *the baseline's incidental peak* rather than the book's **cap**. The cap was 6. So a candidate using 6 of 6 available slots was rejected for using capacity the book demonstrably has. Corrected: the bound is the cap when one is declared, the baseline only when none is. Pinned three ways in the selftest (within-cap allowed, over-cap refused, no-cap falls back conservatively).
- **WHAT THE CALIBRATED SWEEP SAYS, and where it stops.** Direction is robust and monotone — holding tp and hold at shipped values and moving the stop alone: `sl 1.0% → −0.158%`, `1.5% → −0.098%`, `2.0% → −0.034%`, `3.0% → +0.050%`, with drawdown FALLING 40.7% → 26.0% because the tight stop was itself realising the losses. **But it names no value**: every top candidate pins `sl` at whatever grid maximum I set (3%, then 8%), so the optimum is unbounded and the tool says so — `UNBOUNDED: widen the grid before believing a value`. **I stopped there rather than widening again, because widening until a number appears is chasing the artifact, not measuring.**
- **AND THE ACTOR ALREADY EXISTS, which is the useful conclusion.** The Parliament's own tuners already do exactly this: `SWEEP` walks `tp_pct`/`sl_pct`/`max_hold_hr` multiplicatively, replay-gated against a stored candle tape, one lever per bot per cycle, TTL 6h, clamped to `PARAM_BOUNDS`. So **nothing here needs a new mechanism and I changed no parameter.** Two observations for the review instead:
  * `PARAM_BOUNDS["sl_pct"] = (0.005, 0.05)` — the sweep's 8% winner is **outside what the system can express**. Within the cage the answer is the ceiling.
  * The step is **×1.25**, so 1% → the 5% ceiling needs **7.2 consecutive ACCEPTED widenings**, while the improvement only becomes clear around 3%. A single step (1.00% → 1.25%) moves the mean about −0.158 → −0.13: real, but small enough that it may not clear the tuner's own floor. **A correctly-designed hill-climber can still be stuck when its step is small relative to the distance to the useful region** — that is a design observation, independently corroborated by a different instrument on real Lighter candles, and it is the operator's call rather than mine.
- Suite green, five audits green. Read-only throughout: no gate, threshold or parameter moved.

## 2026-07-30 (gu) — THE FLEET'S FIRST EXIT LEVER, and why 🧲 SNAP BACK'S EXIT WAS THROTTLING ITS OWN ENTRY

- **THE ASYMMETRY, quantified**: of the 9 `lighter-books` levers, **0 governed an exit** — every one is ENTRY or CAPACITY. The growth rail could move what all six books OPEN and nothing about what they CLOSE, on a fleet where `(gq)` showed the exit decides the result. Across all 42 registered levers only 8 touch an exit, and every one belongs to the two funding arms or the taker; not one belongs to a Farnham Six book.
- **THE FINDING THAT PICKED THE FIRST ONE.** `(fz)` replaced Snap Back's fixed 150bps entry gate with a percentile of the LIVE residual distribution — a good fix — and then floored that adaptive gate at `EXIT_BPS * ENTER_FLOOR_MULT` = **40 × 1.5 = 60bps**. Measured live this hour across the scout's 90 liquid books: **median 7.9bps, p90 21.8bps, max 50.1bps**. So:
  * the entry floor (60bps) sits **above the p90** of the distribution the gate adapts to, and above the observed max on this sample;
  * the adaptive gate can therefore only ever descend to a bound set by **a stale exit constant nobody re-based** — the same class of defect the adaptive gate was introduced to remove;
  * `(gq)` corroborates from the other side: this book's dominant exit is `long_max_hold`. Positions **time out instead of converging**, because 40bps convergence is outside what the tape delivers.
  **The exit constant is throttling the entry.** That is the concrete form of "entries and exits are one system", and it is why widening the entry alone could not fix this book.
- **REGISTERED, NOT RETUNED.** `disloc.exit_bps` — cage **[8.0, 40.0]**, `step −4.0`, default **UNCHANGED at 40.0**. The cage is *derived from the measurement*, not chosen: `lo 8` ≈ the live median (a target the tape reaches most days), `hi 40` = the operator's current default, so this lever can only ever **loosen the exit toward the observed distribution and never tighten it past where the operator already has it**. Verified after the change: `EXIT_BPS` still runs at 40.0 and the entry floor is still 60bps. **Registering a lever moves nothing** — it makes the constant reachable by the organ that measures the distribution, instead of by me picking a number, which is the same reason `(gr)` declined to register carry's exit levers before its telemetry existed. Here the measurement already exists and is published every 5 minutes.
- **CONSUMED, WITH BOTH SILENT-INERT TRAPS CLOSED.** The lever is read in `apply_tuning`'s loop **and** `EXIT_BPS` is added to `_ENV_DEFAULTS`. The second is not decoration: `apply_tuning` does `_ENV_DEFAULTS[attr]`, and a missing key raises a `KeyError` that the loop's own `except Exception: continue` **swallows** — leaving a lever that is registered, looks consumed, and can never move. It is also what makes an expired lever revert to the operator default rather than ratchet (the `(fz)` bug). Mutation-verified: removing the snapshot entry fails exactly `test_the_exit_lever_is_consumed_and_snapshotted`.
- **FOUR TESTS**, each pinning something that would otherwise regress silently: that the lane has an exit lever at all (every other test would still pass if this one were dropped); that the cage reaches **inside** the observed distribution; that both consumption sites exist; and that `EXIT_BPS` still governs the entry floor — because if that coupling is ever removed, the cage's rationale (derived from the ENTRY side's distribution) stops applying and the note becomes a lie.
- Suite green, five audits green, `--selftest` green. Nothing enacted: `lighter-books` remains an evidence-board-authored lane, and no enactment has been proposed.

## 2026-07-30 (gt) — THE EXIT SWEEP, and the gate that stops it lying to us

- `(gq)` measured which exit reason each book's money *came from* — observational: what the shipped rule DID. `(gt)` is the counterfactual half: `scripts/study_exit_sweep.py` replays a book's OWN trades under alternative exit rules against **Lighter's own hourly candles**. It exists now so it is ready the moment `(gr)`'s telemetry starts filling rows, rather than lagging behind the data.
- **THE METHOD, and the two properties that make it more than a grid search.**
  * **Entries are held constant** — the trades come from the book's real ledger, so the entry side is never fitted and only the exit varies. A joint entry+exit grid on a few dozen trades finds a beautiful rule and means nothing, which is exactly the mistake a *"tailored to perfection"* brief invites.
  * **Throughput is modelled.** The replay is SEQUENTIAL with the book's real position cap: an entry arriving while the book is full is SKIPPED, as the live bot would skip it. Without this a sweep reports *"hold longer, earn more"* while silently ignoring the trades that holding longer prevents — and 🌾 carry and ⚖️ Counterweight are both AT their caps, so for them it is the whole question.
- **ITS FIRST REAL RUN PRODUCED A TEXTBOOK TRAP, WHICH IS WHY THIS ENTRY IS LONGER THAN THE CODE.** On pm-gillard — the only book with prices on every row (238 of 238), so the only one runnable today — the top five rules were **all `sl_pct: None`**, claiming **+2.105%/trade** against the book's real ≈−1.4%. Removing a stop always flatters an in-sample choppy tape: realised losses become unrealised ones and the mean improves while the equity path gets worse. Nothing in the output argued back. Added, immediately:
  * **`max_dd_pct`** — a candidate may not win by DEEPENING the drawdown. (The go-live gate has a 15% drawdown bar; a no-stop rule would breach it.)
  * **`peak_open`** — a candidate may not demand exposure the book cannot carry. A rule needing 40 simultaneous positions is not a rule this book can run, whatever its mean says.
  Both are floors in `_clears`, both mutation-tested, and re-running with the cap at 6 showed the honest shape: the best candidate skips **140 of 238 trades** to get its number. That is not a better exit for this book — it is a different book that trades 40% as often.
- **THE CALIBRATION GATE — the most important thing here.** With the cap applied, the replayed SHIPPED rule scored **+0.030%/trade while gillard's actual ledger mean is NEGATIVE.** *A harness that cannot reproduce what did happen has no standing to say what would have happened.* So `calibrate()` now compares the replayed shipped rule against the book's real ledger mean and, on a gap beyond `SWEEP_CALIB_TOL_PP`, **withholds every recommendation** — `verdict.uncalibrated = True`. **FAIL-CLOSED**: supply no baseline and nothing is recommended at all. Three known divergence sources, all live for gillard: the shipped rule was a GUESS rather than read from the bot, funding accrual is unmodelled, exit slippage is unmodelled. A failed calibration is therefore not necessarily a bug — it is the harness stating that what it omits is big enough to matter for that book.
- **SO THE HONEST OUTPUT TODAY IS "I DO NOT YET REPRODUCE THE BASELINE, TRUST NOTHING."** That is the correct result for a first run and it names its own next step precisely: read each book's REAL exit constants out of its code instead of guessing them, and model funding for the books where it is material. Presenting the +500% total that the uncalibrated version produced would have been the single worst thing I could have shipped today.
- Other honest divergences, in the module header rather than buried: **intra-bar ordering is unknowable** from hourly OHLC, so a bar touching both levels takes the ADVERSE one (biases results DOWN — the opposite assumption is how backtests lie); slippage omitted (OPTIMISTIC — treat a thin margin as none); **one regime** (item 18). **Funding books are REFUSED outright**, not caveated: for 🌾 carry and ⚖️ Counterweight the P&L *is* funding, so a price-path sweep measures the wrong thing and a footnote nobody reads is not a safeguard.
- A grid-edge winner is reported as **UNBOUNDED**, never as a value — gillard's winner sat on the edge for both `tp_pct` and `max_hold_h`, so the correct output was "widen the grid", not "ship 48h".
- **READ-ONLY**; enacts nothing, writes no lever, moves no gate. Registered in the selftest set. Suite green, five audits green.

## 2026-07-30 (gq) — NOBODY WAS READING THE EXIT REASON, and it was in the ledger the whole time

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"optimise and enhance exits on all bots so they are able to open and close as efficiently as our infrastructure and ecosystem."* Entries in this fleet have levers, adaptive gates, a scout, a tuner and a brain. **Exits have constants.** Before changing one of them, one question needs data instead of intuition: *which exit reason is making the money, and which is losing it?*
- **The attribution already existed in the data and no code read it.** Every close carries its exit reason — either in `reason` (the funding/dislocation/index bots) or as the suffix of the `<side>-<lens>_<exit>` tag (the taker, the Parliament). `scripts/study_exit_attribution.py` reads both dialects and reports, per (book, exit_reason): n, total $, mean %, win %, and **median hold**. The hold column is what turns a table into a diagnosis: two exit reasons on one book with a 6x hold difference are not two rules, they are **one rule firing before the other can**.
- **🌾 YIELD HARVESTER — the finding that reframes the fleet's best book.** t=2.58, +$61.12. It earns through `*_decay_paid`: **n=25, +$71.42**, ~100% win, median hold **65–70h**. It loses through the sided flips: **n=47, −$17.32**, 14% and 0% win, median hold **6–10h**. More than half its trades exit via a rule that loses, in a tenth of the time the winning rule takes. Its thesis is "hold until the funding decays and you have been paid"; something is closing it first. **Note the precision that matters for the fix**: a THIRD, unsided `flip` bucket (n=10) is **+$7.02**, so "flip loses" is true only of the sided ones — stating it loosely would send the fix to the wrong branch.
- **THE STOP IS THE FLEET'S DOMINANT LOSS MECHANISM.** Ticket Taker shadow: `*_sl` **n=28, −$37.32** against `*_tp` n=73, **+$47.65** — which is *how that book holds positive dollars (+$6.92) and a negative mean per trade at the same time*, a contradiction that had been sitting unexplained on the dashboard. pm-gillard: `*_sl` **n=78, −$21.11 at a 0% win rate and a 15–19 MINUTE median hold**. A stop that never wins and fires inside twenty minutes is inside the book's own noise: harvesting, not protecting. `*_sl` at 0% win on n≥5 appears on **seven** living books.
- **THE HOLD RATIO SORTS THE FLEET.** New metric (`hold_ratio()`): top-earner hold ÷ top-loser hold. Bucketing the 20 living books:

  | class | n | net | profitable |
  |---|--:|--:|--:|
  | ratio ≥ 3 — winner runs | 4 | **+$62.67** | 3/4 |
  | ratio ≈ 1 — symmetric | 5 | −$2.77 | 1/5 |
  | **SINGLE EXIT** — no ladder | 4 | −$12.90 | **0/4** |

- **AND THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED**: the first bucket is +$61.12 of carry plus three tiny books. So "winners running" is **suggestive, not proven** — reading it as proven would repeat the single-book-drives-the-result error this repo has already made three times (the (gi) era-pooling retraction being the most recent). **The single-exit result is the robust one, because it is structural rather than statistical**: a book with exactly one exit reason has no ladder at all, and none of the four is profitable. `crypto-breakout-4h` and `freqtrade-dad` close ONLY via `long-breakout_donchian_breakdown` — **no take-profit has ever fired on either**. 🎯 Perp Sniper's single lifetime close was a `long_max_hold` timeout, so its TP and SL have never fired at all.
- **RETIRED ROWS ARE EXCLUDED BY DEFAULT AND LABELLED, NEVER SILENTLY DROPPED** — from `cleanup_legacy_bots.LEGACY_BOTS`, the same single source `golive_readiness` uses. This matters more here than anywhere: the ledger is HISTORY, and a Kraken-era book measured **+$272.09**, the largest line in the whole attribution. Reading a live exit rule off it would be reading another venue's tape. A selftest pins that the label changes no number.
- **READ-ONLY.** Measures and prints; changes no gate, writes no lever. Its output is the EVIDENCE an exit change needs under *"never modify bot logic without backtesting first"* — it is **not** permission to make one. Registered in the selftest set, which is how I found I had not registered it: `test_no_unregistered_selftest` failed on the first full run and told me so.

      n=82 · extra.caps = {enter_apr: 0.2, max_positions: …}
  to
      n=71 · caps=None · build=None · equity 1085.96

  and held there across three consecutive samples. `funding_carry_bot.py` emits `caps` **unconditionally** inside its publish payload every loop, so `caps=None` on a live row is proof the winning writer **is not running HEAD** — a publisher predating `(gd)` stomped the good one. That detector is the only reason this was diagnosable from outside a container, and a test now pins that `caps` stays unconditional.
- **WHAT IS NOT DAMAGED — checked, not assumed.** The paper LEDGER for that row is **clean: 82 closes, ZERO duplicate `trade_id`s**, latest close 15:44 UTC. The test that asserted "both are covered" has been replaced by its **opposite**, carrying this whole account, so the next session cannot re-derive the same wrong conclusion from the same true premise (that the repo can't tell which service owns the row).
- **STILL OPEN, AND ONLY THE OPERATOR CAN CLOSE IT**: a deploy rule cannot fix a duplicate that is already running. `yield-harvester-shadow` was `● Online` before the dispatch — the landmine predates me; the dispatch stepped on it. **One of the two services must be STOPPED in Railway**, and until then the row will flap to whichever loops last. Reverting here only stops this repo from re-waking it on every push.
- **THE LESSON, which is not "check service names"**: I reasoned about the cost of a redundant *deploy* and never asked what the two services would both *write*. A duplicate publisher is not a duplicate deploy. When two services can be pointed at one image, the question is not "is redeploying cheap?" — it is **"do they share a key?"**

## 2026-07-30 (gm) — A ROUTING FIX CANNOT DEPLOY ITSELF; and the Farmer's book gate was fail-OPEN on negative prices

### Part 1 — the deploy fix that deployed nothing

- **MEASURED, immediately after merging `(gl)`.** That commit corrected four wrong Railway service names. Run `30495189332` on the merge reported **`Deployed: freqtrade-bots,pnl-dashboard`** — the four corrected rules stayed silent, and the books STILL had not received `(fz)`'s levers, **two merges later.**
- **WHY**: the decide step fires on CHANGED FILES, and `(gl)` touched the workflow, the CHANGELOG, the dashboard and some tests — **not one of the six books' own files, and none of `$_shared`.** Correcting the route does not retroactively travel it. This is a distinct failure from `(gl)`: there the rule was wrong; here the rule was right and nothing rang the bell.
- **FIXED STRUCTURALLY**: `.github/workflows/railway-redeploy.yml` is now part of the six shadow books' own trigger set — in BOTH `paths:` (whether the job runs) and their decide greps (which service) — so a routing fix redeploys the services it routes to. **Scoped to those six deliberately**: $1k shadow books, no volumes, nothing lost to a redeploy, and precisely the ones whose names were unverified. `freqtrade-bots` and the two LIVE services are excluded — the live pair must stay marker-gated, because an unmarked WIP push must never ship real money.
- **THE GUARD BIT ITS OWN AUTHOR, ONE HOUR LATER, AND WAS RIGHT.** My first attempt composed `_shared` from a second variable, which needs double quotes to interpolate — and inside double quotes every `$` anchor must be written `\$`, which is a **literal dollar in the regex, not an end-anchor**, silently turning `bot_pnl_store\.py$` into a pattern matching nothing. `audit_deploy_coverage` refused it outright (*unresolved shell interpolation*), which is the `(gl)` parser fix earning its keep against the person who wrote it. Rewritten as ONE single-quoted literal; the indirection bought nothing. A test now pins that the anchors survive (`bot_pnl_store.py.orig` must NOT match).
- **The dispatched catch-up**: run `30495640709` deploys all six explicitly, because the structural fix only helps the NEXT routing change.

### Part 2 — `book_metrics` had never executed, and hid a fail-open

- **THE HOLE**: across the entire suite, `lighter_funding_bot.book_metrics` executed **only its `def` line**, and the inner `vwap_slip` **not at all** — on stage C of `scan_candidates`, the last gate before a **REAL-MONEY** order and the only place the entry path reads the book. Cause: the bot's own `--selftest` monkeypatches it with a canned dict (`_selftest_explore`), so the real function never ran under any test. 30 tests in `tests/real_money/test_funding_book_gate.py`; lines 905–964 now **fully covered, zero missing**.
- **🔴 THE DEFECT THOSE TESTS FOUND — fail-OPEN on real money, FIXED.** The top-of-book check was `if not bids[0][0] or not asks[0][0]`: falsy for exactly ONE bad value, zero, and **TRUE for every negative one** — while `vwap_slip`, twenty lines below, validates with `if px <= 0`. Two notions of "valid price" in one function. Measured on the live path, an ask level of `[-1.0, 50]` sorts FIRST (asks sort ascending), passed the check, and produced:

      mid 49.0 · spread_bps −20408 · sell_slip −10204 · ask_depth −50

  The caller's gates are `spread_bps > MAX_SPREAD_BPS` (20) and `slip > SCAN_MAX_SLIP_BPS` (25). **A negative number passes both.** So a SHORT on that book cleared every gate in stage C on a garbage mid. Now `<= 0`: **strictly restricting** — it can only reject books it used to accept, and only ones whose best price is not a positive number, which is not a price. No strategy parameter moves, so the backtest-first rule is not implicated. A general test now asserts that ANY dict this function returns has positive mid, non-negative spread, non-negative depths and non-negative-or-None slips — the assertion that stops the next variant.
- **A SECOND FINDING, PINNED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED**: a single **zero**-priced ask level discards the WHOLE book (it sorts first, the check rejects, six good levels behind it are thrown away), while the same garbage on the bid side sorts last and is correctly ignored. Direction is **safe** (returns None, caller vetoes) so no money is at risk — but it is a **silent starvation** path on the live entry gate, and this repo has an expensive history with that shape (🎯 Perp Sniper at n=1 for weeks). Fixing it would **widen** which coins the live bot considers, which is exactly what *"never modify bot logic without backtesting first"* governs. Pinned with a test that flips when the fix lands, so it becomes a deliberate act rather than a refactor side effect.
- **The defensive sort is now proven load-bearing**, not asserted to be: a scrambled book (what a REST snapshot returns — and REST is the Railway norm, the ws being CDN-blocked) must give a byte-identical answer to the sorted one. Remove the sort and the live bot's normal path reports the wrong slippage.
- **THE STUB IS BOUND TO THE REAL SHAPE**: a test asserts the `--selftest` canned dict carries every key the real function returns, so a new key cannot leave the selftest passing while the live path `KeyError`s. That stub is *why* this function had no coverage.

### Part 3 — the 30-day clock, corrected

*(Dated 30-Jul to sit with its `(fz)`–`(gj)` siblings and the operator's Sydney clock; git's UTC clock read 29-Jul at commit time. Noted per the rule-5 convention rather than left to be re-discovered.)*

- **WHAT I FOUND while doing it.** `scripts/golive_readiness.py` implements the `(fk)` bar — **the one rule that decides whether a $1,000 shadow book may ever hold real money** — and it shipped in **no image**, ran on **no schedule**, and published **nothing**. Its verdicts existed for exactly as long as a terminal's scrollback. So between reviews there was no way to see that 🌾 Yield Harvester is passing **five of six bars** and failing only the 30-day window. This repo already has a name for the class: *a rule nobody runs is not a control* — the same shape as the 38 unrun selftests before 18-Jul, and as `--selftest-live` before `(ej)`.
- **IT IS NOW AN ORGAN.** `COPY scripts/golive_readiness.py` into `Dockerfile.freqtrade` (kept at its repo path — the module inserts its parent on `sys.path`, so moving it to `/freqtrade` would insert `/` instead), a 6-hourly `--publish` loop in `run_all.sh`, and a `paths:` entry + service grep in `railway-redeploy.yml`. `audit_image_imports` and `audit_deploy_coverage` both green — it is the only file under `scripts/` that ships in an image, which is exactly why it needed both entries. Publish is **opt-in** (`--publish`), so a bare laptop run against the shared DB still writes nothing: the radar's rule from `(cn)`.

The dashboard used to have no way to show "5 of 6, missing the window" except by string-matching the prose in `fails`, and prose is what drifts. `_selftest` asserts `all(bar_map(s).values()) is grade(s)[0]` **and** that the count of dark chips equals the count of failed bars, over every fixture — the two cannot diverge silently, so six green chips can never sit on a book the gate rejects. `tests/autonomy/test_golive_organ.py` (33 tests) binds the same equivalence plus the dashboard's chip table to `BAR_NAMES` exactly: a renamed bar fails there rather than degrading into a missing chip.
- **AN UNMEASURABLE DRAWDOWN NOW FAILS THE BAR.** The condition was `is not None and >=`, i.e. a book whose drawdown could **not** be computed sailed through the one bar the operator wrote himself. Fail-closed is the only defensible direction on a real-money gate, and it is what makes `bar_map` exactly equivalent to `grade` instead of quietly kinder in one corner. In practice this fires only at `GOLIVE_BOOK_USD=0`, so it changes no current verdict — it removes a way for a future one to be wrong. (The table's `maxDD` column would also have raised a `TypeError` formatting that `None`; fixed in the same pass.)
- **🚦 GO-LIVE GRADER CARD** on the dashboard, immediately after 📡 Edge radar — the radar asks *"is there an edge?"*, the grader asks *"has it earned real money?"*: the same books, the next question. Six chips per book, **closest-to-the-bar first** because the operator's question is "who is next?", with the `(fk)` divergence marked explicitly: **✦** = passes the new bar and the retired win-rate rule would have **rejected** it (the carry shape), **⚠** = the old rule would have **admitted** it. Win% is shown and labelled *reported, not a bar*. The card states that it promotes nothing — a scoreboard that reads like an authorisation is how a shadow book ends up holding real money by momentum. Fail-silent against junk/absent/partial payloads (10 malformed-payload cases), and a payload with no `bars` key renders **all-dark**, never all-PASS.
- **HISTORY, because the question is a TRAJECTORY one.** `save_history` alongside `save_state`: the baseline document asks *"is t moving toward 2.0 and n above 41?"*, which a single current snapshot cannot answer. ~4 writes/day against 60-day retention.
- **READABLE WITHOUT A RAILWAY LOGIN**: `golive-readiness` added to `/bus.json`'s live and history SELECTs and to the vitals watchdog (8h — one missed publish on a 6h cadence). A dark row matters specifically here: it means the operator is reading a frozen real-money scoreboard.
- **Also in this pass** (the same operator ask, smaller): `lever_lane_summary()` so the nine new `lighter-books` levers render as `books carry×2, disloc×1 · live×1 · taker×1` instead of collapsing into a bare integer, wired into both the autonomy card and the vitals row.

## 2026-07-30 (gg) — WHERE THE BRAIN WAS DEGRADING: a retired venue's fee, on a zero-fee venue, suppressing the only diagnosis that can act

- **THE MEASUREMENT FIRST**, because a constant should never be changed on a hunch: all **203 active Lighter books report `taker_fee 0.0000` and `maker_fee 0.0000`** (read live from `orderBookDetails`, 2026-07-30). The venue is genuinely zero-fee — and `is_taker_fee_enabled` is **TRUE** on every book, i.e. the fee machinery is ON and the rate happens to be zero. That last detail is why the fix is not "hardcode 0.0". Suite **406 passed**, 25 floors held, six guards green.
- **THREE DEFECTS COMPOUNDED in `bot_learn`'s round-trip friction estimate:**
  1. **WRONG KEY FORM.** `FEE_RT.get(bot, FEE_RT_DEFAULT)` was called with the **suffixed** row name (`perps-funding-carry-lshadow`) while every table key is a bare base name. **Not one entry ever matched**, so every bot in the fleet fell through to the default. This is the *identical* defect the 23-Jul audit fixed for `ERA_START` — five lines away, in the same function, where `_era_base` already strips exactly this suffix.
  2. **A RETIRED VENUE'S FEE AS THE FLEET DEFAULT.** `0.0052` is Kraken **spot** taker round trip. Kraken was retired 14-Jul. Every Lighter book was being charged it.
  3. **THE VENUE IS ZERO-FEE.** So the phantom cost was not an over-estimate; it was the *entire* estimate.
- **WHY THIS CORRUPTED EVIDENCE RATHER THAN MERELY MIS-REPORTING IT.** `diagnose()` rule 3 fires when `fee_rt / med_loser >= 0.5` and `med_loser <= 0.012`, and it **RETURNS**. At `fee_rt = 0.0052` that condition holds for **any bucket whose median loser is ≤ 1.04%** — an extremely common loss size — so rule 3 pre-empted rule 4, `regime_timing`. And `diag_regime_timing` is the **ONLY** diagnosis kind carrying an actuator (`regime_gate`, `main()`). **The brain was structurally unable to recommend the one thing it is able to act on**, and instead told the operator to "raise band/edge floors or move venue" over a cost of zero. The 28-Jul audit's observation that 4 of 12 live diagnoses read `fee_bleed` was this, visible and unexplained.
- **THE FIX — MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, so it cannot rot back:**
  - the scout publishes the venue's own schedule (`lighter-market.fees`: max taker/maker across active books — **max, not mean**, because a cost estimate should be conservative and one expensive book must not hide behind 200 free ones);
  - `bot_learn.fee_rt_for(bot, venue_fees)` is the **single owner**. A Lighter row uses the measured schedule (`taker × 2` — a taker-only estimate is optimistic for a round trip) and **can never inherit a non-Lighter default**;
  - a dark scout falls back to a declared Lighter constant (`0.0002`), deliberately **not 0.0**: an unmeasured fee must not become a claim of certainty either. It is small enough never to trip rule 3 on a realistic loser, and honest about being an estimate;
  - `main()` LOADS the block and THREADS it into `diagnose()` — without both halves this would have been another fed-by-nobody consumer, silently taking the fallback forever while the docstring claimed "measured".
- **`tests/autonomy/test_brain_fee_basis.py` — 33 tests, and the ones that matter are behavioural, not arithmetic:** that the phantom constant DOES trip rule 3 at a 1% loser while the measured fee does not; that `diagnose()` end-to-end now reaches `regime_timing` on a zero-fee venue where it previously returned `fee_bleed`; that a **genuinely fee-paying** venue still earns `fee_bleed` (the fix must not blind the rule); that a **fee hike at the venue reaches the diagnosis with no code change** — the self-correcting property that makes the "measured" claim real; and that `main()` both loads and threads the feed.
- **A FIXTURE MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING, because it is now the fourth of its kind this session.** My first cut of the end-to-end test used **epoch ints** for `open_ts`; `bot_learn._epoch` is `datetime.fromisoformat`, so every trade failed to match a regime snapshot, `regime_matched` came back **0**, and the bucket fell to `mixed_unclear`. The test would then have "passed" its no-`fee_bleed` assertion while proving **nothing** about `regime_timing` — the actual claim. Caught by printing the evidence block instead of trusting the green. Note the real dialect is *mixed*: trade rows carry ISO strings, regime history carries raw epoch floats, in the same function — spelled out in the fixture's comment so the next reader does not rediscover it.
- **WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS.** Every diagnosis the brain has published on a Lighter book since 14-Jul was computed against a 52bps phantom. Those verdicts are not retroactively fixable — but from the scout's next publish the diagnoses are computed on the venue's real cost, and the `regime_gate` actuator is reachable for the first time.

## 2026-07-30 (gf) — THE LEDGER THAT NEVER FORGOT, and the listing date that was on every row all along

- Continuing the audit's open list. Suite **373 passed**, 25 floors held, six guards green. Every item verified against the source (or the live venue) before being changed.
- **MY OWN `(ga)` FIX HAD A SLOW-ACTING VERSION OF THE BUG IT FIXED.** `surge_done` was a monotone SET: every book the sniper offered — as a surge OR as a young book — was excluded **forever**. Over weeks both new candidate sources decay to silence, which is precisely the starvation `(ga)` set out to remove, just on a longer fuse. A surge is an EVENT, not a permanent property of a book.
  - Now `{sym: last_offered_ts}` with a **cooldown** (`SNIPER_SURGE_COOLDOWN_H`, default 168h): a book that surged a fortnight ago and surges again is a genuine new event. `active_done()` returns the still-live set and **prunes in place**, so the persisted payload cannot grow without bound either. Restore accepts the `(ga)` list format and stamps those entries NOW rather than dropping them — a restart must not re-offer the whole venue at once.
  - `not_young` stays PERMANENT and that is deliberate: books only ever age, so that one is a true monotone fact. The distinction between "a fact that cannot reverse" and "an event that must expire" is the whole fix.
- **THE LISTING DATE WAS ON EVERY BOOK ROW AND THE FLEET THREW IT AWAY.** `orderBookDetails` carries `created_at` (epoch ms) for all ~202 books, in the response the scout ALREADY fetches every cycle — while the sniper burned **4 candle REST probes per loop** to approximate the same fact from a bar count. Measured against the live venue: majors read **558.6 days**, and exactly **4 books sit under 21 days** — so "young" is now an exact, venue-sourced number instead of a slowly-converging proxy.
  - The scout publishes `ages_d`; the sniper prefers it and keeps the probe cache as the fallback for a dark scout. The probe list now excludes anything `ages_d` already answered, **so once the scout redeploys the candle probes stop entirely** — the fallback costs nothing when it is not needed.
  - **A book whose timestamp will not parse is ABSENT from `ages_d`, never 0.** "Age unknown" must not read as "brand new", which would hand the sniper every unparseable book as a debut candidate. Pinned by a test.
  - `build_snapshot` gained an injectable `now_ms` rather than reading the wall clock, so `ages_d` stays offline-testable. My first cut referenced a `now_ms` that did not exist in that scope — an AST check caught the `NameError` before it shipped.
- **TWO NEW IMMUNE INVARIANTS on the surfaces `(fz)`/`(ga)` created:**
  - **`n_liquid == 0` on a FRESH scout** — the shape that silently starves the **LIVE Ticket Taker**: every lens builds its tickets from `liquid`, so a zero there publishes a perfectly healthy-looking payload with an empty opportunity set and the live arm simply stops entering. `n_liquid > n_books` already caught the *impossible*; nothing caught the merely CATASTROPHIC.
  - **`vols` truncation and negative turnover** — that map is what `fleet_bus.scout_universe` ranks, so it now decides what FIVE books trade, and no organ asserted anything about it. The dangerous shape is not an ABSENT map (every consumer reads empty as "keep my configured list") but a fresh, **truncated, non-empty** one, which silently re-points five books' orders at a sliver of the venue. Flagged below 50% coverage of `n_books`.
  - Both selftested in BOTH directions: the fixtures fire, and a healthy payload — including one with NO `vols` key, the documented fail-safe — stays silent.
- **STILL OPEN**, unchanged and named rather than quietly dropped: the brain's `FEE_RT` is keyed on bare bot names with a RETIRED venue's spot fee as its default, on a venue this repo documents as zero-fee (4 of 12 live diagnoses read `fee_bleed`, and that rule shadows the only rule with an actuator); and the six books remain outside `fleet_risk`'s EXPOSURE view — deliberately NOT in the long budget, where shadow books would compete with real strategies for the veto.

## 2026-07-30 (ge) — THE AUDIT'S REMAINING FINDINGS: a "widening" that CUT the ticket supply 25%, two levers inert at their consumer, and a two-sided book reporting its shorts as longs

- The 9-agent organ audit finished. `(gc)` acted on the first two readers; this is the rest. Every item below was VERIFIED against the source before being fixed, and two of the audit's own claims were checked and one design point disputed. Suite **369 passed**, 25 floors held, six guards green.
- **THE WORST ONE — the scout tuner was CUTTING the ticket supply every cycle and logging it as a widening.** `TOP_N_LADDER`'s default was hardcoded `os.environ.get("SCOUT_TICKET_TOP_N", "6")` and `(fz)` moved the scout's own default to **12**. So the tuner computed its ladder position from 6 and "widened" to 9 — a **25% CUT** to the candidate supply feeding the fleet's only measured alpha (shadow short-divergence, +3.035%/trade vs regime, t=+4.04), every cycle, described in its own log as growth. **Its selftest asserted `== 9`, i.e. the test was holding the bug in place.**
  - Fixed at the ROOT, not the value: the ladder's default now reads `fleet_tuning.LEVERS["scout.ticket_top_n"]["env_default"]`, and `(gd)`'s `audit_lever_bounds.py` keeps THAT equal to the scout's real code default on every push. The class is now closed rather than the instance fixed.
  - Both tuner assertions rewritten to pin the RULE ("the first rung above whatever the default is", "one notch deeper than that") instead of the literal rungs. A test frozen to a number follows the bug; a test written against the rule follows the fleet.
- **TWO LEVERS WERE INERT AT THEIR CONSUMER — both mine, both from `(fz)`:**
  - **`fundspread.k` / `fundspread.universe_n`**: `apply_tuning()` was called ONCE at boot, before the loop. The board could author `fundspread.k`, proprioception could grade it, and the running container would never see it until a redeploy. K now refreshes every loop (UNIVERSE_N stays boot-only ON PURPOSE — widening the universe mid-run would rank coins whose funding history was never backfilled).
  - **`xp.funding.min_vol` / `live.funding.min_vol`**: registered in `(fz)` and **read by nobody** — the Farmer's `MIN_VOL` was a bare env read. The judge could have promoted the floor, stamped the promotion, and the real-money liquidity gate would never have moved. **A promotion that reports success while changing no behaviour is worse than an absent lever: it manufactures false evidence for the next decision.** Now consumed in `apply_levers()` with `min_vol` in `_ENV_BARS`, so expiry reverts to the operator's number. Verified end-to-end: a lever of 2e6 moves `MIN_VOL` to 2e6.
- **A SIGN BUG IN AN ENFORCED CAP, which my own widening is what activates.** Snap Back is TWO-SIDED (`is_long = dev_bps < 0`) but published `"held": sorted(meta.keys())` — a bare LIST. `fleet_risk.held_items` maps a list to side `""`, and `""` classifies as **LONG**. So Snap Back's SHORTS were counted as longs in the per-symbol pileup cap, which ships `mode=enforce` and is consumed by the family bot — **a Snap Back short could veto a family LONG entry on the same symbol.** Latent while the book held nothing; the 30-Jul gate re-base (150bps → ~60) and universe widening (16 → 40) are precisely what make it trade. Fixed at the publisher with the same dict contract Counterweight and the sniper already use, and pinned by a test that asserts the OLD shape mis-signs and the NEW one does not.
- **REFUTED, and worth recording as such:** the 20-slot long budget is NOT saturated by the widening (measured 13/20 GREEN; none of the six widened books feed `fleet_long`), so no budget change was warranted — the same conclusion `(gb)` reached independently. Two organs agreeing on a refutation is worth more than either alone.
- **A DESIGN POINT I DISPUTED.** The audit recommended book verdicts be HELPING/NEUTRAL only, citing the module rule that HURTING exists only where a real paired $ counterfactual does. I kept HURTING, deliberately: `grade_book`'s counterfactual is the book's own pre-episode window — the SAME shape `grade_live` uses for `live.funding.*`, which does emit hurting. And the failure directions are asymmetric: a false HURTING on a $1k shadow book reverts one widening (restrict-first, the safe direction), while a MISSING hurting lets the author widen into dilution forever, which is the exact failure the grader exists to catch. Verified no reach into real money: `fleet_tuning._live_hurting` keys on the `lighter-live` lane only, and the verdict strings stay inside the set `fleet_immune` accepts.

- **STILL OPEN, named rather than dropped:** the scout throws away `created_at` — the exact answer the sniper now burns 4 candle probes per loop to approximate; no organ asserts any invariant on the new `vols` map, which now decides what five books trade; `n_liquid == 0` is unchecked and would silently starve the live Taker's whole ticket supply; the brain's `FEE_RT` is keyed on bare bot names with a RETIRED venue's spot fee as its default, on a venue this repo documents as zero-fee; and the six books remain outside `fleet_risk`'s exposure view (deliberately NOT in the long budget).

## 2026-07-30 (gd) — THE CAGE MUST FIT THE VALUE: 33 of 42 levers had no machine-readable default, and the registry had already drifted from the code

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"if the bounds don't correlate properly then recalibrate individually and have each supporting asset correspond, correlate and optimise."* Suite **367 passed**, 25 floors held, every guard green — now six guards, not five.
- **THE FINDING.** A lever is THREE things that must agree: the registry CAGE (`lo`/`hi`), the DECLARED default, and the `os.environ.get` default the consumer ACTUALLY runs. Only the cage was ever machine-readable. **33 of 42 levers carried their default in PROSE inside the `note` field**, and the consumer's real value lived in a different file entirely — so nothing could compare the three, and they had already drifted: `(fz)` moved `scout.ticket_top_n` 6 → 12 in code and its registry note still read *"default 6"* the same afternoon. That is not cosmetic. Every organ that reasons about a lever's HEADROOM — the board's step ladder, the judge's candidate queue, the authority census, a human reading the cage — reasons from the number the registry states. A registry that misdescribes the running value is worse than no registry.
- **RECALIBRATED, INDIVIDUALLY.** All 42 levers now carry a machine-readable `env_default`, each one read from its consumer's own `os.environ.get` call rather than guessed. Measured result: **no default sits outside its cage** and **no cage is degenerate** — so the bounds themselves were sound; what was missing was the ability to KNOW that. Twelve levers are one-sided (default pinned at a bound) and that is reported rather than failed, because it is usually correct: an emission bar sitting at its most restrictive end has all of its room in the growth direction.
- **`scripts/audit_lever_bounds.py` — the new CI guard, and the drift arm is the point.** It enforces (A) every lever has a machine-readable default or a DECLARED exemption, (B) that default lies inside its own cage — a default outside means the very first `get_lever` clamps it, silently changing behaviour nobody asked for, (C) **the registry default MATCHES the consumer's real code default**, parsed by AST from the consuming file, (D) no degenerate cage, and (E) every book lever's `step` actually moves inside the cage and terminates — a step of 0 is an author that can never act. **Mutation-verified end to end**: drifting `SCOUT_TICKET_TOP_N` 12 → 9 in the code while leaving the registry at 12 produces exactly one named failure and nothing else. Negative fixtures cover all five classes. Wired into `changelog-check.yml` and registered in `ENFORCED_AUDITS`.
- **SATURATION IS NOW OBSERVED, NOT INFERRED.** The `(gb)` author judged "is this book at its cap?" from occupancy against the cap the REGISTRY believed it had enacted. Those can legitimately differ — a bot that has not redeployed, a quarantined lever, a TTL that lapsed between the write and the read — and the book's own number is the one that actually gated its trades. The three capacity books now publish `extra.caps`, and the author PREFERS the published cap, falling back to the registry only when absent. Without this an author could judge saturation against a cap it set itself and the bot never adopted, and talk itself into widening forever.
  - **A guard caught me publishing the wrong number.** My first cut published carry's raw `ENTER_APR` — the HL-denominated constant `main()` is explicitly forbidden to touch, because it is the 8x-basis defect. `_selftest_basis` failed the build. The payload now carries `_enter_apr`, the basis-corrected bar the arm actually gates on. The guard was right and the fix is the honest one.
- **WHY THIS IS THE COMPOUNDING PIECE.** `(fz)` gave the books levers, `(ga)` gave them a deploy route, `(gb)` gave them an author and a grader, `(gc)` fixed the auto-revert ratchet that would have made every widening permanent. Each of those is a link. This entry makes the LINKS CHECKABLE: from here a lever cannot be registered with bounds that do not bracket its value, cannot drift from the code its bot runs, and cannot carry an author step that does nothing — and CI says so on every push rather than a reader noticing months later.

## 2026-07-30 (gc) — THE AUTO-REVERT RATCHET: (fz) broke the growth rail's central safety property on all six books, and the new grader was born inert

- **HOW THIS WAS FOUND.** An 8-way parallel organ audit (proprioception, evidence board, immune/regen, fleet-risk, brain, judge/incubator, scout/tuner, dashboard) against the `(fz)`/`(ga)`/`(gb)` tree. It CONFIRMED the authored-by-nobody suspicion `(gb)` had already fixed, and then found **three defects in my own just-shipped work** plus two pre-existing dark consumers. Suite **366 passed**, 25 floors held, every guard green.
- **DEFECT 1 — THE ONE-WAY RATCHET, and it is the serious one.** Every `apply_tuning()` `(fz)` shipped did `cur = globals()[attr]` and then `tuning.get_lever(lever, cur)`. `get_lever` returns its **`default`** when a lever is absent, expired or quarantined — so passing the ALREADY-MOVED value meant a widened lever **could never come back**. Auto-revert-on-expiry is not a nicety here, it is the growth rail's stated central safety property (`fleet_tuning` docstring: *"levers EXPIRE back to defaults on their own, so auto-revert is the resting state, not a feature to remember"*), and `(fz)` broke it on all six books simultaneously. It was inert only because `(gb)` had not yet given the lane an author — the two commits together would have armed it. Fixed by snapshotting `_ENV_DEFAULTS` at import in all six bots and handing THAT to `get_lever`. Pinned by a test that moves a lever, expires it, and asserts the revert; the mutation that restores `cur` turns it red.
- **DEFECT 2 — `sniper.apply_tuning()` had NO CALL SITE.** Defined, registered, tested at the unit level, and invoked by nothing: `grep apply_tuning lighter_perp_sniper.py` returned only the `def`. `sniper.surge_mult` could never reach the bot. Now called at the top of the scan loop, and a test asserts EVERY book's `main()` contains a call site.
- **DEFECT 3 — `grade_book` was BORN INERT, which is the exact class it was written to fix.** It read `ep.get("lever")`; a real episode carries **`stance`** (a `{lever: value}` dict) and has no `lever` key at all — as `grade_scout` already knew (`next(iter(ep["stance"]))`). So `bot` was always None and it would have returned `"unmapped-lever"` forever. **My selftest passed because the fixture invented an episode shape the tracker never produces.** Same root cause as the `(gb)` hurting-key bug and the `(fz)` scout-accessor bug: *I keep testing my own invented shape instead of the real contract.* Three times in one session. The fixtures now use the tracker's real shape, and an explicit assertion (`"lever" not in _real_ep`) turns red if it ever regresses.
- **DEFECT 4 — `lever_verdicts` had no branch for book levers.** A perfectly graded book episode produced NO verdict, so no consumer hook — the board's hurting-refusal, the tuner's skip — could ever fire. The grader would have been a dead end even once it graded. Added at the shadow-lane floor (`basis: "book-paired"`), with a test that walks a hurting verdict all the way to `hurting_levers()`, the accessor the board actually reads.
- **PRE-EXISTING, and both silently dark on every HEALTHY cycle:**
  - **The evidence board never FETCHED `fleet-radar`, `parliament` or `parliament-tuning`.** All three are read via `_g()`, but they were absent from `_keys`, and `_g` returns `_b.get(k) or {}` whenever the batch read SUCCEEDS. So the radar's per-book edge classification — the senior corrective on the naive promotion screen, the one that calls the Yield Harvester's +$58 headline an `artifact` — and the entire Parliament section were inert, and only worked when `fetch_states` FAILED and `_g` fell through to per-key loads. A consumer that works only when its own fast path breaks.
  - **`EP_CAP` was a global FIFO.** A burst of ungradeable `recorded` episodes could evict GRADED ones, and graded rows are the only ones `lever_verdicts` can use — including live-lane rows whose verdicts revert a REAL-MONEY lever. Six new book lanes make that burst likely rather than theoretical. Graded rows now hold the budget first; recorded rows fill what is left, chronological order preserved.
- **THE CAPACITY-LEVER METRIC, restated because the audit pushed back on it and the pushback was right to raise it.** `grade_book` asks a different question of capacity levers than of selection levers, and the reason is `grade_live`'s own recorded lesson: `live.clip_scale` is MATHEMATICALLY invariant to per-trade `pnl_pct`, so it fails closed. A capacity lever is NOT invariant — carry prices each trade against a per-position NOTIONAL constant — but demanding a HIGHER mean would reject every capacity widening that ever worked, because a ranked selector reaching deeper takes worse names by construction. So the bar is **"did quality HOLD while throughput rose?"**, with dilution as the detectable failure. That is the honest question for the lever's actual job.
- **STILL OPEN, stated rather than quietly dropped:** four audit readers (immune/regen, brain, judge/incubator, scout/tuner, dashboard) had not returned when this landed. The known-remaining items from the two that did: no book PUBLISHES its effective cap, so the board infers saturation from occupancy alone and cannot distinguish "at the cap" from "at the cap it set itself last cycle"; and the six books are invisible to `fleet_risk`'s EXPOSURE view (deliberately NOT added to the long budget — shadow books must never compete with real strategies for the veto).

## 2026-07-30 (gb) — THE LOOP CLOSES: the books' levers get an AUTHOR and a GRADER, and two dead guards found by asserting against the real payload

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"make every organ integrate with the new information ... grow into what works."* `(fz)` gave six shadow books levers and `(ga)` gave them a deploy route. Both ends of the LEARNING loop were still open — and an open loop is the thing this fleet keeps shipping by accident. Suite **354 passed**, every guard green.
- **THE AUTHOR — the `lighter-books` lane was authored by NOBODY.** `(fz)` bound the lane to the evidence board in `AUTHOR_LANES`, and nothing in `evidence_board.py` wrote it: `board_levers` was populated only from the gapscout ladder (INERT since Gap Scout retired 17-Jul) and `live.clip_scale`. Verified by reading the write site, not assumed. So nine registered, consumed, tested levers **could never move**. That is the exact mirror of the registered-but-not-consumed class, and it would have looked healthy forever.
  - `synthesize_books()` is the missing author, and it is deliberately narrow because a widening author that fires on noise is worse than none: **SATURATED** (holding AT its cap ⇒ turning away already-graded candidates) widens the capacity lever ONE step; **STARVED** (0 open AND no new closes for `BOOK_STARVED_H`) loosens the gate lever ONE step; anything else proposes nothing. A book that is working is left alone.
  - Guards, each selftested: never re-assert a lever graded HURTING; one step per book per cycle; at the registry bound it says nothing; **a MISSING ROW proposes nothing** — absence of evidence must never read as "widen", which is what stops a publish outage ratcheting every book wider on every cycle.
  - The starvation clock needs memory a single snapshot cannot provide, so the board persists `books: {bot: {closed, ts}}` and **restarts the clock only when the close count actually moves**. A missing row KEEPS the prior memory rather than resetting — otherwise a DB blink would restart every window.
- **THE GRADER — book episodes were RECORDED and never judged.** `group_of()` sent them to `other:carry`, and `grade_episode` returns `{"status": "recorded"}` for that, so the tuner's hurting-refusal and the board's helping-walk could never fire for these books. `grade_book()` closes it, and the interesting part is that it asks **two different questions**:
  - **SELECTION levers** (a gate, a ranking, a universe) change WHICH trades are taken, so "did per-trade return improve?" is well-posed.
  - **CAPACITY levers** (more concurrent slots) are where `grade_live`'s hard-won lesson applies but **does not transfer wholesale**. `live.clip_scale` is MATHEMATICALLY invariant to per-trade `pnl_pct` (the clip cancels top and bottom — measured, one distinct value across the whole range) and therefore fails closed. A capacity lever is different: carry prices every trade against a per-position NOTIONAL constant (`funding_carry_bot.py:467`), so the metric does not cancel — but the COMPOSITION changes, because slots 9..12 hold the 9th..12th best candidates. So the honest question is **NOT "did the mean rise"** (it should not; a ranked selector reaching deeper takes worse names — demanding a higher mean would reject every capacity widening that ever worked) but **"did quality HOLD while throughput rose?"** DILUTION is the real failure mode of widening a ranked book, and it is detectable.
- **TWO DEAD GUARDS, both found by checking the payload instead of trusting my own fixture. This is the same mistake `(fz)` recorded for the scout accessor, caught the same way, and it is worth stating that it recurred:**
  1. **The hurting-refusal was reading a key that does not exist.** I wrote `prop_state.get("hurting_levers")`; `fleet_proprioception` publishes `verdicts: {lever: {"verdict": ...}}` — the shape `synthesize_proprioception` in the SAME FILE already reads. The set was always empty, so the single most important guard in the author — never re-widen a lever that measured worse — was silently dead. **My selftest passed because the fixture invented the same wrong key: I tested my mistake, not the contract.** Now asserted against the real shape, plus a symmetry case (a HELPING verdict must NOT block a widening, or the rail freezes permanently).
  2. **`grade_book` would have been structurally incapable of ever grading.** `run_once` fetches `feeds["trades"]` only when an episode's group is in `("live-clip", "live-funding", "live", "xp")` — a `book:*` episode never triggered the fetch, so the grader would have returned "recorded" forever. Wired, tested, and inert. The selftest now asserts the predicate names book groups, so the mutation that removes it turns the test red.
- **ALSO:** book levers gained machine-readable `env_default` + `step` in the registry (the author's ladder arithmetic was otherwise guessing at values documented only in prose), and the ladder rounds — `1.6 - 0.2` is `1.4000000000000001`, which both reads badly in the payload and drifts as steps accumulate, since the no-op check depends on a step landing exactly where the last one left off.
- **VERIFIED AND NOT CHANGED:** the six books are absent from `fleet_risk.FREQTRADE_BOTS`, so `(fz)`'s widening (carry 8→12, Counterweight 10→16 legs, Index 3→10) does **NOT** consume the fleet's 20-long budget and cannot make the risk layer veto the family books. Adding them to that budget would be actively harmful — shadow books would compete with real strategies for the veto. Their invisibility to the EXPOSURE view is a genuine (advisory) gap and is left for the next pass rather than fixed blind.

## 2026-07-30 (ga) — THE BOOKS THAT DO NOT TRADE: the sniper's trigger was unobservable, six services could not auto-deploy, and 7 configured symbols do not exist

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"We cannot have bots not making trades ... the sniper needs its scope fixed ... find and implement whatever auto deploys necessary so that changes can be implemented in real time."* Suite **354 passed**, 25 floors held, every guard green.
- **FIRST, THE ONE THAT INVALIDATED THE LAST COMMIT: six services had NO AUTO-DEPLOY RULE AT ALL.** `lighter_dislocation_bot`, `lighter_funding_spread_bot`, `lighter_index_bot`, `lighter_perp_sniper`, `lighter_trend_bot`, `lighter_family_bot` shipped only when a human ran `railway up`. That applied to `(fz)` **itself** — its levers, widened universes and adaptive gate would have sat in main, green, tested, and reached **no container**. This is the fleet's documented "code was right and was never running" class, and it was sitting under the whole offense pass. All six now have `paths:` entries AND service greps, including the SHARED modules each image carries (`bot_pnl_store`, `paper_broker`, `venues/`, `fleet_tuning`, `fleet_bus`, `funding_basis`) — `(fz)` added `fleet_tuning`/`fleet_bus` to five of these images, so without the shared-module rule the very levers it registered could never have reached them.
  - **HONEST GAP, and it needs one look after the first run:** these services' exact Railway names could NOT be verified from this repo — the only names recorded anywhere are `funding-carry`, `pnl-dashboard`, `market-context` and the two live bots. Hardcoding a guess would red-fail the build (the "Service not found x3" mode the workflow already documents). So the deploy step now **RESOLVES each target against `railway service list`**, reports an unresolvable name as a loud `::warning::` and skips it instead of failing the run, and **prints the real service list** — which is how the next session fixes any name in one pass, with data rather than another guess.
- **THE SNIPER'S SCOPE — the trigger was UNOBSERVABLE, not wrong.** `new_listings` is a market-set **DIFF**: a symbol qualifies for exactly the ONE loop in which it first appears, and only if the process is running with a warm baseline at that exact moment. Miss that loop — a deploy, a restart, a venue hiccup — and the listing is in `baseline` forever. That is why the book has **n=1 close in weeks** with `new_listings: []` on the bus. The thesis (violent repricing in a book with no settled history) was never the problem.
  - **`young_candidates()` — the third source, and the one that actually reaches.** A book with `<= SNIPER_YOUNG_MAX_BARS` (21) daily candles is in the same debut regime and stays observable for **weeks**. Measured on the venue for calibration: the majors carry **~402 daily bars**, so a handful of bars is unambiguous. Ordered YOUNGEST first (closest to the debut, where the move is), filtered on real turnover (`YOUNG_MIN_VOL_M` — a debut with no volume is a ghost print, and this bot's own history is full of one-sided debut books), deduped against the same ledger the surge source uses, bounded per loop.
  - The candle probe is **GOVERNED** (`YOUNG_PROBE_BUDGET=4`/loop, the venue REST budget is shared) and **MONOTONE**: a book measured past the young bar enters `not_young` **permanently**, because books only ever age. So the probe cost decays to zero once the venue has been walked once, and the cache is safe to persist.
- **SCOPE HYGIENE — 7 configured symbols DO NOT EXIST on Lighter.** Measured against the live venue with `ctx.supports()`: **family core 2/15 dead (ATOM, ALGO)**, family WIDE 4/29 (ATOM, ETC, ALGO, INJ), **Counterweight 5/30 dead (INJ, RUNE, STX, GALA, W)**. Typed when the venue carried a different set, never re-checked. Dead names cost a backfill call each, make `len(COINS)` a lie in every log line, and on a book that needs `2*K` rankable coins to rebalance at all they can be the difference between rebalancing and skipping. `prune_dead()` now drops them at boot and NAMES them in the log. **Fail-safe direction matters here and is tested: a `supports()` that RAISES KEEPS the coin** — an unreachable venue must never silently empty a book's universe, which would be this same commit causing the exact disease it is treating.
- **A HYPOTHESIS I CHECKED AND WAS WRONG ABOUT, recorded because the check is the point.** I expected the near-zero books (mum 0 closes, crypto-swing-daily 1, avo-maria 4) to be starved by insufficient candle history — SwingDip needs `min_bars=230` and `SPAN_BARS['1d']` is 240, a 10-bar margin. Measured instead: **the majors carry 402 daily bars**, so history is not the binding constraint for the family's core universe. The `min_bars` margin is still thin enough to be worth knowing, and the measurement is what produced the sniper's 402-bar calibration — but the family books' low turnover is NOT a data-availability bug and must not be "fixed" as one.
- **A REAL BUG THE NEW TESTS CAUGHT BEFORE MERGE:** `young_candidates` coerced symbols with a bare `str(sym)`, so a `None` key became the string `"NONE"` and would have entered the snipe pass as a tradable-looking candidate. Fixed at the function (`isinstance(sym, str)`), not at the test.
- **TESTS: 40 -> 49** in `tests/autonomy/test_book_levers.py` — the young-book cohort (ordering, turnover floor, dedup, bounds, junk), the probe cache's governed-and-monotone construction, and `prune_dead`'s never-empty-a-book-on-a-venue-error contract.

## 2026-07-30 (fz) — THE OFFENSE PASS: six books get levers, five get the venue's real universe, and the fleet's tightest supply cap doubles

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"optimise all bots, enhance their integrations ... every bot needs every tool at its disposal and every bot needs the ability to grow."* This is `(fy)`'s ranked list, implemented. Suite **345 passed** (was 305), **25 coverage floors** held (was 19), every guard green.

"The ability to grow" is not a metaphor: it is registry membership PLUS a consumer that actually reads it, and they had neither. New lane **`lighter-books`** (author: evidence board only — it gains NO new reach into real money; the judge remains the sole writer of `live.funding.*`), nine levers, each consumed by an `apply_tuning()` called every loop.
- **THE SUPPLY CAP — `SCOUT_TICKET_TOP_N` 6 → 12.** `strategy_tickets` truncates EVERY lens to this number, and on the live bus `dip` and `divergence` both returned **exactly 6** while breakout/momentum returned 5 — a lens returning exactly its cap is a lens whose cap binds. The lens behind it is the fleet's only measured alpha (shadow short-divergence **+3.035%/trade vs its own regime, t=+4.04**), and it was being handed a 6-wide candidate list from which to fill 4 slots. Every "closed question" on the Taker (`TT_MAX_OPEN`, `TT_DIV_GAP`, lens on/off, clip size, symbol eligibility) was about **ALLOCATING** that fixed supply; **none of them was about ENLARGING it.** Widening moves no entry bar — the taker's own gates still judge every ticket.
