A ranked selector cannot pick a winner it never sees, and unlike loosening a gate, enlarging the candidate set does not weaken the selection rule at all. The scout already scans every book each cycle, so this is a read of work already done.
  - **A REAL BUG CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED, recorded because the class matters:** the first cut of this accessor read `marks[sym]["vol_m"]` and `stress["med_bps"]`. The scout's actual payload is `marks = {sym: PRICE}` (a float) and `stress = {..., "med": ...}` — so the accessor would have returned an empty universe and a permanent `None` stress **against every real payload**, while its own selftest passed on a fixture I had invented. Caught by diffing the fixture against the LIVE `/bus.json`. The selftest now asserts against the scout's real key names, and the scout publishes an explicit public **`vols`** map (the data existed only in `_marks`, documented as a private diff base no consumer should bind to). The accessor still falls back to `_marks` so a consumer shipped ahead of the scout's next deploy is not dark.
  - **CONTRACT, and it is the important part:** any doubt returns `[]`/`{}`/`None`, and **every caller must read empty as "keep my configured list", never as "trade nothing"**. The widening is an ENHANCEMENT, never a DEPENDENCY — no organ outage may shrink a book's universe. Tested per consumer against a dark bus, a stale bus, a RAISING bus and a born-dark import.

  - 🌾 **Carry `MAX_POSITIONS` 8 → 12** — measured at **7 open of 8**: the fleet's biggest earner was one slot from full and turning away carries it had already graded. Its 38.8% win rate is not a defect; carry's return lives in the tail, which is exactly why refusing graded candidates is expensive.
  - ⚖️ **Counterweight `K` 5 → 8, universe 30 → up to 60** — measured **AT its structural cap**: 10 open = exactly K=5 × 2 legs. It still takes exactly top-K/bottom-K, now from a real cross-section.

Universe 16 → 40 (dislocations are commoner in thin books — exactly where the hand list had no coverage).

Widened sleeves reuse the ALREADY-VALIDATED rules (200-day band for index-like, 20/50 cross for single names and commodities), so the change is one variable, not two.

Ranking by funding costs nothing, changes no entry gate, and points the one free choice this book makes at the signal class that actually earns.

Its event (a brand-new listing) is too rare to grade: **n=1 close in weeks**, and `new_listings` is routinely empty. A strategy that cannot accumulate a sample cannot be validated, improved, or retired on evidence. **The subtlety, which is why this needed its own ledger:** every surging book is ALREADY in `baseline` (seeded with all active markets), so baseline cannot dedup this source the way it dedups listings — without the persisted `surge_done` set a surging book would re-enter `pending` every loop forever. ## 2026-07-29 (fw) — THE CAPTURE GAP IS EXPLAINED AND ~0% RECOVERABLE: it is slot luck and a censoring artifact, not skill the live arm is missing

- **THE QUESTION `(fs)` OPENED.** Same era, same ticket stream, live **+0.883%/trade** vs shadow **+3.484%**. That 2.601pp gap looked like the biggest prize on the book. It is not: **~13% is recoverable at the absolute most, and realistically ~0%.**
- **THE DECOMPOSITION**, in per-trade percentage points of the 2.601pp gap:

  | cause | share | $ over the 5.2d window | recoverable? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **slot-saturation LUCK** — the shadow skipped tickets because it was FULL, not because it chose better | **55.8%** (+1.451pp) | $1.74 | **$0 — not a defect** |
  | **CENSORING artifact** — the shadow's wider bars keep losing positions OUT of its closed-trade ledger | ~13% | ~$1.25 | **not money** (-0.89pp once open positions are marked to market) |
  | stop width (live -0.03 vs shadow -0.04) | 30.6% (+0.797pp) | $0.96 | only by widening a real-money stop — **already refuted `(fo)`** |
  | take-profit height | (+0.198pp) | $0.24 | **negative standalone** — raising tp without the stop makes live worse |
  | FILLS / SLIPPAGE | — | **-$0.16** | **REFUTED, and backwards: live fills CHEAPER** |
  | ENTRY TIMING | — | +$0.19 (one SKHY case) | **REFUTED** — live enters later but at a BETTER price |
  | FUNDING | — | +$0.03 | live IS receiving it, it IS in the ledger, ~zero both arms |
  | **CLIP SIZE / the $40 cap** | — | **~$11.85 of the $15.01 total** | **STRUCTURAL — a $66 book cannot be a $1k book** |

- **THE THREE HYPOTHESES I WAS MOST CONFIDENT IN ARE ALL DEAD.** I proposed fills, entry timing and funding capture as the likely causes. Fills run the *other way* (live is cheaper by $0.16), live's entry timing gets a *better* average price, and funding is being collected and recorded and is ~zero for both arms. Recording that plainly because "the live arm must be getting worse fills" is exactly the kind of plausible story that survives on plausibility alone.
- **THE CENSORING FINDING IS THE SUBTLE ONE and it generalises beyond this book.** A wider bracket does not only change outcomes — it changes WHICH positions have closed yet. The shadow's losers were still open and therefore absent from its closed-trade mean; marking them to market costs it **-0.89pp**. **Any live-vs-shadow comparison between arms running different bars is biased in favour of the wider-barred arm** until open positions are included. That is a standing methodology hazard for the experiment judge's paired bar, not a one-off.
- **WHAT IT MEANS.** The live arm is NOT leaving skill on the table — it drew worse symbols in a 10-trade sample and its twin's ledger flatters itself by deferring losses. Combined with `(fu)` (configuration closed, ~455 configs) and `(fv)` (inversion is drift, but short-divergence has real alpha), **every route to more realised profit that does not require capital or time is now measured and closed.**
- **SIDE FINDING, unresolved and worth a look:** a shadow stop fired on a mark the fill disagreed with (~$0.42 on that trade; excluding it moves the shadow mean 3.484 -> 3.635%). Not gap-driving, but it means a stop can fire on a price the book never traded. Logged in the handoff.
- Read-only research. No lever, no bar, no book, no real money.

## 2026-07-29 (fv) — "IF IT LOSES, IT CAN WIN" — TESTED, and it is the falling market. But the same test found the Taker's edge is REAL ALPHA, not drift

- **THE OPERATOR'S IDEA, taken seriously and measured.** *"Think outside the box — if it loses, it can win."* The arithmetic is sound: a loser worse than twice the round-trip fee inverts to a winner, because `inverted = -r_net - 2f`. Swept across every lens/side the Taker has ever traded, exactly one candidate cleared the bar: **inverting `long-dip` gives +1.082%/trade at t=+2.48 on n=13** (not the naive +1.162% — flipping pays the fee twice).
- **AND IT IS THE REGIME, not an edge.** Lighter's tape is one falling-BTC market, so a LONG-biased lens loses BY CONSTRUCTION and inverting it just shorts a falling market — CLAUDE.md item 18, which the repo has asserted since 21-Jul but never measured. The test: subtract the MEDIAN return of taking the same direction in every liquid Lighter book over the SAME window.

  | candidate | raw | vs short-everything | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | inverted `long-dip` | +1.082% (t=**+2.48**) | **+0.098% (t=+0.14)** | **DRIFT** |

  The benchmark column shows why: over those same windows, shorting anything earned +1.75%, +2.33%, +2.89%, +3.03%. **Nearly all of the "edge" was the market falling.** A serious-looking candidate, killed by the right test.
- **THE SAME TEST VINDICATES THE LIVE POLICY, and this is the strongest result of the day.** Subtracting the drift makes short-divergence STRONGER, which is the signature of genuine cross-sectional selection rather than beta:

  | book / lens (current era) | n | raw | vs-market | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | shadow `short-divergence` | 10 | +3.484% (t=+4.86) | **+3.035% (t=+4.04)** | **ALPHA** |
  | live `short-divergence` | 11 | +0.883% (t=+0.73) | +1.223% (t=+1.11) | positive, under-powered |
  | shadow `long-breakoutup` | 8 | -1.973% | -0.828% (t=-0.61) | no alpha |

  Across ALL history the same lens is `n=95, vs-market +0.347%, t=+1.23` — so **the alpha is specific to the post-bull-flip era**, consistent with `(fs)`'s 57-trade losing prior and with the gate being the mechanism.
- **A USEFUL NEGATIVE that changes how `dip` should be read**: `long-dip`'s raw `t=-2.66` looked like a significantly BAD lens. Against the benchmark it is **+0.173%, t=+0.36** — dip has no negative alpha either. It simply went long in a falling market. Nothing about dip is anti-predictive; it is direction-exposed. That is a materially different verdict from "dip loses" and it should be quoted that way.
- **SHIPPED: `scripts/study_alpha_vs_regime.py`** — the instrument item 18 has needed since 21-Jul. Direction-matched benchmark (benchmarking a short against a long market would credit the strategy with the whole drift), MEDIAN not mean (a handful of 1000-scaled meme books would otherwise set the bar alone), refuses to invent a market below 20 quoted books, sample-stdev t per `(fs)`. Selftest discriminates **all four** cases — drift with a huge raw t, genuine skill, NEGATIVE alpha, and the thin-cross-section refusal — because a detector that can only say "no alpha" is not a detector. Verified to reproduce both live findings end-to-end.
- **WHAT THIS MEANS FOR "MAKE IT WIN".** The strategy is not the problem: it has measurable alpha over its own regime. Configuration is closed (`(fu)`: ~455 configs, zero survivors). Inversion is closed (this entry). **What is left is sample and size** — the live arm is n=11 with vs-market t=+1.11, directionally consistent with the shadow's t=+4.04 but not yet significant on its own. More closes fix the first; only capital fixes the second, and the operator's own gate wants 30 days before that conversation.
- Read-only research + one new script. No lever, no bar, no book, no real money.

  | POST-bull (current policy) | 12 | **+0.464%** | 11 of 12 SHORT-divergence |

  The losses belong to long-divergence — **the exact lens the bull gate exists to exclude.** The gate worked; the grading did not.

  | LIVE arm | 11 | +0.883% | +0.77 | +14.71 / **-5.00** pp |
  | SHADOW twin | 10 | **+3.484%** | **+5.13** | +19.51 / +15.33 pp |

- **[CORRECTED, same day, by an independent regrade — "the edge is real" OVERSTATES it, in five specific ways.]**
  1. **ddof.** Every t above used POPULATION stdev. Sample stdev: live **+0.73** (not +0.77), shadow **+4.86** (not +5.13), pooled **+2.79** (not +2.86).
  2. **The "zero shared rows" separateness test was a FALSE NEGATIVE.** Minute-exact matching finds nothing because the arms open the same ticket 1-2 minutes apart. ## 2026-07-29 (fq) — THE DASHBOARD'S HEADLINE AND THE STRATEGY'S EDGE CAN DISAGREE IN SIGN, and the go-live gate reads BOTH bases at once

- **THE MEASUREMENT.** `lighter-ticket-taker-lshadow`, n=135 closes: `/pnl.json` reports **+$6.93** — and the equal-weighted per-trade series sums to **-12.52pp** (mean **-0.093%/trade, t=-0.39**). Same book, same trades, **opposite signs**. The live arm's two bases happen to agree (-$0.18 / -0.183%/trade), which is exactly why the disagreement went unnoticed on the twin.
- **THE MECHANISM — sizing, not edge.** Implied stakes on this book run $20-$80 (median $26). The 51 winners average a **$48.3** stake; the 84 losers average **$36.1**. Winners are sized **1.34x** the losers, so a book that loses on the average trade still books a positive dollar total. That is the constant-risk sizer doing its job (smaller clips where the stop is further away), so the dollar figure is not *wrong* — but it is a statement about SIZING, and it is being read as a statement about EDGE.
- **THE GATE READS BOTH BASES AT ONCE** (`scripts/golive_readiness.py` `stats()`, measured not inferred): `mean` and `t` come from `pct` (equal-weighted, `r[0]`); `h1`, `h2`, `max_dd_usd` come from `pnl_abs` (dollar, `r[1]`). So one book can **PASS "both halves positive" on dollars while FAILING "mean > 0" on percentages** — and the shadow taker does exactly that right now (halves +$4.57 / +$2.36, mean -0.093%). "Both halves positive" therefore does not mean what a reader assumes it means; on this book it is carried by the sizer.
- **NOT CHANGED, DELIBERATELY.** The go-live bar is the operator's rule and was re-specified by him on 29-Jul; picking a single basis is his call, not a session's. Both bases are defensible (dollars are what the book earns; percentages are what the strategy earns) and the mix may even be intentional. This entry makes the behaviour EXPLICIT so the 4-Aug review can decide with the ambiguity in front of it, rather than discovering it inside a promotion.
- **CORRECTS (fm).** That entry cited *"shadow +$7.33 / 135 closes against live -$0.42 / 25 closes"* as the OUT-OF-SAMPLE corroboration for moving the live arm's bracket to the twin's bars. On the equal-weighted basis the twin is **negative** (-0.093%/trade, t=-0.39), so that corroboration does not hold and the argument was weaker than stated. `(fo)` had already reverted the change on independent grounds (the no-interior-optimum artifact); this removes its remaining support rather than changing any outcome.
- **THE GENERAL RULE, worth more than this instance.** A dollar total answers "what did the book earn"; a per-trade mean answers "does the strategy have an edge". When stakes vary they are different questions and can have different answers. **Quote the basis with the number, always** — and when citing a book as evidence FOR a strategy change, cite the equal-weighted series, because that is the one the change is about.
- Publish-only: no code, no lever, no book, no real money. The `/pnl.json` figure is unchanged and remains correct for what it measures.

## 2026-07-29 (fp) — THE AUTONOMOUS TUNER WAS RE-DERIVING THE ARTIFACT (fo) HAD JUST REVERTED: the stop is pinned and can no longer become a lever

- **THE FINDING, and it is a self-repair failure rather than a tuning question.** `(fo)` reverted `TT_SL=-0.04` off the real-money Ticket Taker at ~10:30 UTC because the replay cannot price a stop on a tail-free tape. At **10:46 UTC** `/bus.json` showed `fleet-tuning` carrying `taker.sl = -0.04`, `set_by: scout-tuner`, `expires 12:46:15Z` — **re-enacted every cycle**. The growth rail was autonomously walking back to the exact value the operator's own doctrine had just ruled void, and it would have kept doing so indefinitely on a 2h TTL.
- **VERIFIED IN THE SHADOW ARM'S OWN DEPLOYED FRAME** (bull on, tp .06, hold 72h, max_open 6, $50 clips, 200h/2397-snapshot Lighter tape) — not inherited from `(fo)`'s live-path measurement, re-run here because a different frame is a different surface:

  | stop | net $ | closed | wr % | # sl exits |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | -0.02 | -19.34 | 41 | 22.0 | 21 |
  | -0.03 | -15.10 | 31 | 29.0 | 12 |
  | **-0.04 (what the tuner enacted)** | **+9.81** | 22 | 45.5 | 4 |
  | -0.06 | +22.26 | 22 | 59.1 | 1 |
  | -0.12 | +30.05 | 21 | 61.9 | **0** |
  | **NO STOP** | **+30.05** | 21 | 61.9 | **0** |

  Monotone to the degenerate limit, no interior optimum, and the ladder simply stops changing once no stop ever fires. `SWEEP_SL` was running inside this surface every cycle and, by construction, choosing the widest value in its grid.
- **THE FIX — remove the actuator's authority over a knob its own instrument cannot measure.** Two independent protections, each separately asserted so removing EITHER turns the suite red:
  1. `SWEEP_SL` is now **single-valued**, pinned to the taker's env-default stop (`TUNER_SWEEP_SL` restores a grid). The sweep still runs — it optimises TP and HOLD as before — it just never proposes a different stop.
  2. `STOP_LOSS` has **no entry in `attr_to_lever`**, so a stop cannot become a `fleet-tuning` lever even if the grid is widened again later. The levers comprehension now skips an unmapped attr (`if a in attr_to_lever`) rather than raising, since the sweep's candidate dict always carries all three keys.
- **RESTRICT-ONLY, SHADOW-ONLY, ZERO REAL MONEY.** `taker.*` levers live on the `lighter-taker` lane, which is the **$1k shadow** book; only `live.*` levers steer the live arm, and this touches none of them. It removes a capability, never adds one.
- **EXPECT THE SHADOW ROW'S HEADLINE NUMBER TO FALL** — on this tape from +$29.90 at `-0.04` to about +$14.77 at `-0.03`. That drop is the artifact being removed, not edge being lost, and it should not be read as a regression. Second-order benefit: the shadow arm stops being a moving target, which is a precondition for it ever serving as the experiment judge's control arm.
- **WHY THIS IS THE ONLY CHANGE SHIPPED FROM AN 11-AGENT OPTIMISATION CAMPAIGN.** The campaign's own verdict is that the taker is **capital-bound, not edge-bound**: the live arm holds $66.45 behind a $40 notional cap at ~$10 a clip, so even its measured per-trade rate is worth roughly **eleven cents a day**. Graded by the fleet's own `golive_readiness.py` against the real ledger, the live arm is `n=25, mean -0.183%/trade, t=-0.26, halves -$0.47/+$0.30` — it fails five of six go-live criteria, so there is no edge there to tune into. **[CORRECTED (fs): that pooled ACROSS the 24-Jul bull-mode flip. Era-split, the CURRENT policy is POSITIVE — live short-divergence n=11 +0.883%/trade, shadow twin n=10 +3.484% t=+5.13, pooled t=+2.86 both halves. The edge is real; the book is capital-bound, not edge-dead. Nothing (fp) refutes is affected — the stop artifact is dead for unrelated reasons.]** Every widening candidate was refuted. The one defensible action was to stop an autonomous organ from re-arming a known artifact.
- **Tests**: 3 new assertions, each mutation-verified (re-widening `SWEEP_SL`, restoring the `STOP_LOSS` mapping, and making the comprehension raise instead of skip all turn the tuner selftest red). Suite green; born-dark 20, venue-purity 89.

## 2026-07-29 (fo) — THE EXIT-BRACKET CHANGE IS REVERTED: its evidence was the (fj) artifact, caught by an adversarial test I should have run BEFORE shipping

- **WHAT HAPPENED.** (fm) shipped `TT_TP 0.06 / TT_SL -0.04 / TT_MAX_HOLD_H 72` to the real-money Ticket Taker on a window-sensitivity table that looked strong (the twin's bars beat the deployed bars at every window, both halves positive at every window). Within the hour an independent adversarial agent extended the stop ladder PAST the edge of the grid I had swept, and the result kills it. **Reverted to the operator's deployed `0.04 / -0.03 / 48`.**
- **THE TEST THAT KILLS IT — extend the ladder to NO STOP AT ALL** (live path, tp .06, hold 72h, $10 clips, 200h tape). Re-measured myself, not taken on the agent's word:

  | stop | net $ | n | wr % | # sl | worst trade | worst MAE |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | -0.02 | +1.14 | 42 | 31.0 | 29 | -4.01% | -3.93% |
  | -0.03 (deployed) | +4.14 | 34 | 47.1 | 18 | **-5.08%** | -5.00% |
  | -0.04 (shipped by (fm)) | +7.83 | 21 | 76.2 | 4 | **-7.42%** | -7.34% |
  | -0.06 | +9.22 | 18 | 88.9 | 1 | -7.42% | -7.34% |
  | -0.12 | +9.51 | 16 | 93.8 | 0 | -3.35% | -8.46% |
  | **NO STOP** | **+9.51** | 16 | 93.8 | **0** | **-3.35%** | -8.46% |

- **THE SIGNATURE, and it is one this repo already named TODAY.** Net climbs to the no-stop limit with no interior optimum — the textbook *"a wider stop stops realising losses that later revert"* artifact that **(fj)** identified and withdrew this same morning on the incubator's STOP_LOSS signal. I read the -0.04/-0.05 pair as a PLATEAU and declined the argmax on that basis. It was not a plateau; it was noise on a monotone climb, and declining the argmax gave the reasoning a rigour it did not have.
- **THE DECISIVE DETAIL: there is no tail in this window for a stop to cut.** With NO stop the worst realised trade is **-3.35%** — SMALLER than the deployed -3% stop's own worst trade (-5.08%) and less than HALF the -0.04 candidate's (-7.42%). On this tape the stop does not protect against the tail, it MANUFACTURES the realised loss: every adverse excursion reverted inside the hold. So the instrument cannot price a stop at all, and **every** `TT_SL` verdict drawn from it is void — the grid's, the agent's, and (fm)'s alike.
- **WHY REVERT RATHER THAN KEEP AND WATCH.** Widening a real-money stop is risk-INCREASING and it now has no supporting evidence. The honest asymmetry: a wider stop looks better on a tail-free window BY CONSTRUCTION, and this window is measurably tail-free. Reverting restores the operator's own configuration, which is the correct default when the case for changing it collapses. TP and HOLD went back with it — their sweeps were noisy (no clean shape at any stop setting) and were run at stop settings whose effect dominates them, so nothing in that bracket was independently supported.
- **WHAT SURVIVES, stated so the finding is not thrown out with the number.** `-0.03` IS measurably the worst point on its own surface, and its 72h window fails both halves. That is a reason to DOUBT the deployed stop — not a validated replacement for it. The right instrument is the experiment judge's paired live-vs-shadow bar, not an env dispatch off a replay that cannot price the knob. Queued as a review item, not shipped.
- **PROCESS — the actual lesson, and it is the same one twice in one day.** (fm) was itself a retraction of (fl) for asserting a change without checking the receipt. (fo) is a retraction of (fm) for asserting a change without running the adversarial test that the repo's own doctrine already prescribes and that (fj) had demonstrated hours earlier on the very same knob. Both were caught, and both were caught by measurement rather than by review — but in each case the check existed and was run one step too late. **The sweep is not the evidence; the sweep plus the test that would falsify it is the evidence.**
- The `(fn)` side-aware lens veto is UNAFFECTED and stands — it is an entry-gate correctness fix with its own mutation-verified tests, and the same adversarial agent independently named the entry veto (not the exits) as the binding constraint on the book.

## 2026-07-29 (fn) — THE TAKER IS NOT UNDER-TUNED, IT IS SWITCHED OFF: the live arm has been unable to take ANY entry for 33h, vetoed on a population it does not trade

- **THE FINDING.** The live real-money Ticket Taker's effective allowed-lens set is **EMPTY**, and has been since 2026-07-28T02:40Z (~33h, 28 consecutive brain runs). `allowed_lenses("lighter_live")` is `{divergence}` (hard allow-list) and the brain's lens veto — which is SENIOR and applied on top — currently vetoes `divergence`. Empty set means the entry loop skips every ticket. `/pnl.json` corroborates: `open_trades: 0`, last live entry 28-Jul 00:43Z. **No amount of tuning matters while the gate is shut**; this is why the taker is not "taking off".
- **THE MECHANISM — the veto grades the wrong population.** `bot_learn.grade_scout_lenses` sign-flips shorts (so it is direction-aware in SIGN) but aggregates per LENS, not per (lens, SIDE) — and `divergence` emits both directions. Meanwhile `TT_BULL_MODE` (on since 24-Jul) restricts BOTH taker arms to `(divergence, short)` + `(breakout/breakoutup, long)`. So the arm is judged on a book that is **69% long** while it trades **only short**. Re-derived on the 200h tape with the brain's OWN `episode_firsts` and sign convention:

  | population | eps4h | ehit4h | eavg4h % | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | divergence POOLED (what is published + vetoed on) | 1006 | 0.483 | -0.093 | **VETO** |
  | divergence / **long** (69% of episodes) | 692 | 0.470 | -0.199 | veto — correctly |
  | divergence / **short** (what the arms trade) | 314 | **0.513** | **+0.139** | would NOT veto |
  | divergence / short / **crypto** (what the LIVE arm trades) | 158 | **0.525** | **+0.289** | would NOT veto |

  The losing long majority drags the pooled grade under the hard 0.500 bar and takes the winning short side with it. The lens the live arm is restricted to is the one the pool is killing.
- **THE FIX — grade the sub-population the arm actually trades.** `grade_scout_lenses` now ALSO publishes a nested `by_side` block per lens (same field names as the lens level, episode fields only, so a consumer can hand either dict to the same reader). Every existing field keeps its exact meaning — **no current consumer changes behaviour**. `lighter_ticket_taker.vetoed_lenses` gains an optional `sides` map (lens -> the ONE side this arm may take, derived from `BULL_LENS_SIDES` by the new `restricted_sides()`); when a `by_side` grade exists for that side AND meets the same floor, the verdict comes from it.
- **NOT A LOOSENING — it cuts both ways, and the test proves it.** An arm restricted to a side that grades BADLY inside a HEALTHY pool now gets vetoed where it previously was not. That assertion is in the selftest specifically so this cannot decay into a one-directional widening.
- **FAIL-SAFE to the pre-(fn) rule in every degraded case**: no `sides` (the tuner and the incubator pass none — both unchanged), no `by_side` block (a brain that has not redeployed yet), an unmet sub-floor, or the kill switch `TT_LENS_VETO_SIDE_AWARE=off` all fall back to the pooled grade byte-for-byte. Deploy order therefore does not matter: whichever of brain/taker lands first, the other side degrades to today's behaviour until both are up.
- **MEASURED END-TO-END against the live bus payload**: before, `vetoed = [breakout, divergence, momentum]` and the live allowed set is EMPTY; after, `vetoed = [breakout, momentum]` and the live allowed set is `[divergence]`. **The SHADOW arm gains `divergence` too** — stated plainly rather than buried, because it is a widening of a $1k book: bull mode restricts the shadow arm to short-divergence as well, so the same correction applies to it by the same argument (and short-divergence is that book's best lens, +$15.64 of a +$5.11 book).
- **THE HONEST LIMIT.** The un-veto rests on a POINT estimate. `divergence/short` Wilson lower bound is 0.477 and `short/crypto` is 0.474 — both still under the 0.500 bar. The veto rule reads the point estimate (that is its existing design, unchanged here), so the sub-population clears it, but this is "the pooled grade was measuring the wrong thing", not "the short side is proven good". n=314 / 158 episodes on ONE 200h tape in ONE falling regime.
- **Tests**: 5 new taker assertions + 7 brain checks, each mutation-verified (killing the side-aware branch, dropping the sub-floor check, ignoring BULL_MODE in `restricted_sides`, dropping the `by_side` emission, and mis-keying the side bucket all turn the suites RED). Suite 304 green; born-dark 20, venue-purity 89.
- **Credit**: surfaced by a multi-agent taker-optimisation workflow; every load-bearing number here was re-derived independently against the shipped code before anything was changed.

## 2026-07-29 (fj) — the incubator searches BEYOND the cage, and the first cage signal it produced was FALSE

Operator: *"proceed"* on going past the registry bounds. The search now covers the out-of-cage space — and the first thing it did was try to talk me into widening a bound on an artifact, which is the part of this entry worth reading.

- **Why searching out-of-cage is safe, and the reasoning must survive**: the incubator has **no actuator**. Its only consumer is the dashboard (verified — nothing outside `pnl_dashboard.py` reads `bot_state['strategy-incubator']`). The `fleet_tuning` cages bound what the SCOUT TUNER may ENACT; they were never a bound on what this organ may MEASURE. Clamping the search to them bought no safety and cost the entire out-of-cage question.
- **What IS at risk is confusion, not money**, so: every genotype is stamped `enactable`; the published **champion and the gametes are drawn only from the enactable subset**; out-of-cage results are published separately as `frontier`. `is_enactable` fails CLOSED (unknown gene or unclampable value ⇒ not enactable).
- **`RESEARCH_GENES`** extends each grid a step or two past its bound (~900 genotypes under today's vetoes, a full sweep in ~24s). Kill switch `INCUBATOR_RESEARCH=off` returns the search to the cage exactly.
- **THE FALSE POSITIVE, and the fix.** `cage_analysis` v1 flagged **STOP_LOSS** as binding: the best in-cage stop sat ON the −0.04 bound and −0.06 beat it (net 12.86 → 16.34). Adversarially checked before reporting it, and it does not survive — mean net improves **monotonically** as the stop widens across all 180 configs per value (**−15.10** at −0.015 → **−2.37** at −0.06). That is the textbook "a wider stop stops realising losses that later revert" artifact, the same shape that produced and then WITHDREW the funding STOP verdict — and **even the widest stop is mean-NEGATIVE**, so the bound was never what stood between this book and an edge.
- **The bar is now champion-grade**: a cage may be called binding only if the out-of-cage winner is positive, has a positive **lower bound**, AND is positive in **both halves**. A max over 900 candidates with a positive lcb is still the winner's curse `rank()` exists to avoid — measured: **17 of 900 genotypes are both-halves-positive and every one has a negative lcb**, so nothing in the research space clears the bar. All four genes now read `cage_may_bind: false`, which is the correct answer rather than a missing feature. The raw numbers are still REPORTED, never hidden.
- **A mutation found the safety property was call-site-deep.** Passing the unfiltered `scored` list to `select_elite` survived the whole suite, because no selftest can see `run_once`'s argument. The enactable rule now lives **inside `select_elite`**, where no call site can opt out ([[a-kill-switch-must-reach-the-consumer]]) — re-tested: passing an unfiltered list is now harmless, removing the rule from the function is killed.
- 6 mutations total, each red on its named assertion. Suite 304; five guards green (incl. the new `audit_changelog_letters`). Publish-only — no lever, no book, no row, no real money.

## 2026-07-29 (fc) — the incubator searches the WHOLE legal space, not 11 points around one genome

Operator: *"give it everything it needs to explore every option possible."* It turned out not to need more budget — it needed a search that could reach more than one dimension.

- **THE BLOCKER, measured before building.** `seed_population` emits the default genome plus its single-gene AXIS PROBES — it never varies two genes at once. The only thing that explored interactions was `breed()`, which returns `[]` when the elite is empty; `select_elite` demands `both_halves_pos`, and **nothing on this tape clears it**, so the elite IS empty and the population collapsed to **11 axis probes per cycle**. Gene interactions were unreachable by construction, permanently, on any negative surface.
- **And the budget was never the constraint**: one `evaluate()` is **~32ms** on the 2200-snap tape, so the old cycle spent **~0.4s of an hourly 3600s loop** — four hundredths of one percent.
- **`explore_slice()` (new, pure, selftested)** enumerates the JOINT gene product deterministically and walks it with a persistent **cursor**, covering a bounded slice per cycle and wrapping — so successive cycles sweep the entire legal space instead of resampling one neighbourhood. Measured on the live tape: the legal space under today's vetoes is **144 genotypes; the axis probes reached 11 (7.6%)**. The full space now scores in **3.7s** and coverage is published (`exploration.coverage_pct`), because a search that cannot be seen sweeping is indistinguishable from one that has silently stopped — the (f7cad49) explore-zero lesson.
- **It immediately found what the old search could not see: the best genotypes vary TWO or THREE genes at once.** Top of the full sweep is `{DIP_RANGE 0.05, MAX_HOLD_H 48, STOP_LOSS −0.04, TAKE_PROFIT 0.03}` — three genes off default, structurally unreachable by axis probes.
- **And the exhaustive result is a much stronger negative than the old one: 0 of 144 genotypes are both-halves-positive.** That is no longer "we did not find an edge" but "there is no edge in the legal space on this tape". Best full-window net is +$4.16 with h2 −10.25 — the same one-sided shape every other measurement this session found.
- Register stays durable: only the ranked **top 24** of a sweep land in it, or one cycle's population would fill the cap and evict every dormant entry. The cursor deliberately does NOT advance on a cycle that scored nothing, so a dark cycle cannot skip a slice it never measured.
- **A mutation caught a weak test of mine**: the determinism check compared two calls in ONE process, which passes even with `set()` ordering. The cursor has to mean the same genotype next hour in a FRESH interpreter, so enumeration is now pinned structurally (sorted names, first varying fastest) — `set()` and reversed order are both killed. 4 mutations total, each red on its named assertion.
- Also registered `scripts/audit_secret_leak.py`, which landed in `f6d7a2a` (fb) without its `SELFTEST_MODULES` entry and was failing the rot guard for anyone who pulled. Suite **304 passed**; four guards green. Publish-only — no lever, no book, no row, no real money.

## 2026-07-29 (fb) — a secret can no longer reach a commit; and the default scanner was blind to the exact credential that leaked here

Operator asked for hardening beyond Bitdefender + LuLu. This is the repo half: the local pre-commit catch plus the CI backstop. No bot, no lever, no row — tooling only.

- **`scripts/audit_secret_leak.py` + `.gitleaks.toml` + `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` (all new).** Fifth guard in `changelog-check.yml`, same shape as the other four: a positive run and a `--selftest` negative fixture. gitleaks 8.30.1, pinned and **checksum-verified for all four platforms**; an unpinned platform is REFUSED, not installed with a warning (`audit_sdk_pin` doctrine).
- **MEASURED, and it is the whole reason this is not just `useDefault = true`: gitleaks' DEFAULT ruleset scans a full Postgres connection URI carrying an inline password CLEAN.** That is precisely the credential class that leaked here — a live Postgres URL accumulated into `.claude/settings.local.json` (which stores approved commands VERBATIM) and was one `git add .` from permanent. Four custom rules added for what the default set misses: `db-connection-uri`, `private-key-block`, `aws-access-key-id` (a bare `AKIA…` also scans clean), `railway-token`.
- **The first draft of the allowlist was BROKEN, and its own selftest caught it.** It matched the whole LINE against words like "example"/"masked", so a live GitHub PAT trailing `# example config` sailed straight through — the attacker, or a careless paste, controls the comment. Fixed to match the SECRET ITSELF; the bypass is now a permanent regression fixture. Mutation test went 3/8 → **8/8**.

A new AWS key or DB URL in the same file still fails the commit. The guard's own fixtures are exempted PER LINE (`gitleaks:allow`), never by path, so a real secret pasted into the guard is still caught.
- **End-to-end verified, not assumed**: staged a Postgres URL, `git commit` was BLOCKED, nothing landed. Working tree scans clean (84 raw findings → 0, all triaged, none silenced). `.git/hooks` is untracked, so the hook cannot ship by committing it — hence the installer script and the CI job for any clone or `.claude/worktrees/` sibling that never runs it.

## 2026-07-29 (fa) — the incubator stops hoarding duplicates and corpses; and the honest answer on "fresh options": there are none in-cage

Operator: *"learning from the incubator so it doesn't make or duplicate bots that don't achieve anything, dead genotypes disposed of and fresh new models and options to test."* Three asks; the first two were real defects and are fixed, the third is answered with measurements rather than invention.

  - **IMMORTAL CORPSES — the worst of the three.** Cap eviction sorted dormants by `best_lcb`, a HIGH-WATER MARK, so one lucky historical score outranked every recently-measured genotype forever. Ranking is now on the LATEST reading, with entries scored this cycle ahead of any dormant.

Fail-safe throughout: never retires on unknown staleness, on a genotype scored this cycle, below the cycle floor, or on a positive latest reading; and the whole pass is skipped on a short tape (no scoring, no disposal). Disposal is REPORTED on `register_hygiene`, never silent.

## 2026-07-28 (dz) — LIVE-MONEY surface hardening from the full-fleet audit: the Farmer's deposit double-count (phantom halt), the unchecked ':live' boot restore (durable state wipe), the same-loop conviction cap under-count, and four smaller truths

- **D1 DOUBLE-COUNT (lighter_funding_bot).** The boot/day-roll `day_start_equity = account_value()` goes through the EquityGuard, which can ACCEPT a deposit/withdrawal on that very read and buffer it — so the captured baseline is already capital-INCLUSIVE. The first loop then popped that same buffered move and shifted the baseline AGAIN (`capital_adjusted_day_start`): deposit D → day_start=E+2D vs equity=E+D → a phantom 'loss' of D, and a D ≥ 10% of book FLATTENS + HALTS the live book on the operator's own deposit. Fixed: the buffered moves are folded into the ledger immediately after any FRESH capture that survives boot (tracked via `_baseline_is_boot_read`; a PERSISTED pre-move baseline restored over the capture keeps the shift, which is then the correction) and after the day-roll capture. The taker already had this ordering (fold before adopt, no shift on the adopt path) — one rule, both live bots.
- **':live' BOOT RESTORE now CHECKED ([[load-state-seeds-durable-state-on-a-failed-read]], the whole blob this time).** The 22-Jul fix hardened the quarantine read; meta/explore_seen/initial_equity/capital_adjust still came through the UNCHECKED `load_state`. One boot-time DB blip wiped every position's max-hold clock/entry bars/conviction clip/explore src, re-based `live_baseline` to current equity on the first loop (lifetime P&L → zero), zeroed the D1 capital ledger — and the next save made it all DURABLE. Now: ONE checked read with the quarantine's own bounded retry; a genuinely failed read boots DEGRADED (`live_state_blind`): NEW entries blocked, the ':live' save suppressed (never overwrite a blob we failed to read), baseline adoption refused, and an in-loop self-heal re-reads until clean (halt record senior on heal). The exact `quarantine_blind` pattern, one shelf up.
- **SAME-LOOP CONVICTION CAP UNDER-COUNT (lighter_funding_bot).** `open_notional` prices a position in `pos` at its meta clip but a same-loop open counted only in `open_now` at the FLAT clip — so the 2nd open of a loop under-counted the 1st by up to (conviction_hi−1)×order_usd ≈ $30 at hi=2.2: a cap breach armed for the day conviction promotes to live. Fixed: a successful open is inserted into `pos` immediately (counts MORE notional, never less). Selftest pins the $126-vs-$90 shape.
- **Smaller truths, same pass:** Farmer W/L now counts wins on TOTAL P&L (price+funding) on the flatten path and counts them AT ALL on the blind-stop path (a profitable stop_blind close always published as a loss); the Taker's halted-day state save carries `sl_block` again (every halted cycle was erasing the post-stop cooldown stamps) and pages on a failed write; `implementation_shortfall.arm_drift` keeps the NEWEST row per bot (the judge passes DESC paper_trades rows — the old dict-comp graded each arm by its OLDEST close, masking current drift and asserting stale drift); `fleet_bus.stake_multiplier`'s docstring stops claiming "reduce-only" (two-way since 21-Jul).
- Tests: Farmer 8/8 + judge + impl-shortfall + bus selftests green; full suite 200 passed; born-dark / deploy-coverage / venue-purity / sdk-pin green. ## 2026-07-25 (dt) — REFUTED on LIGHTER: the funding-slope gate is an HL-only edge; making its history durable (the Phase-2 "fix") would HURT the losing book (operator: "backtest the fix first")

- **The measurement that had never been run.** The Farmer's slope gate ("enter only while |apr| still BUILDING, >= 1h ago") is validated ONLY on Hyperliquid (`backtest_funding_leverage.py`: +1.3%→+8.4%, both halves) — `backtest_funding_lighter.py`'s own line ~156 said it was "not modelled" here. Added an OPTIONAL slope gate to that Lighter sim (default OFF → the existing sweep verdict is byte-identical, CONFIRMED against the default run) in three modes: `off` / `durable` (always active — the proposed fix) / `failopen` (live reality: ~11 restarts/day × 1h ≈ 46% of hours the gate is OFF). Mirrors the live `_slope_ref` exactly — the funding TAPE is the history (`apr 1h ago = m["fund"][t-3600]`), and a missing value FAILS OPEN, since a real tape gap IS the restart gap. Merged cleanly with the concurrent (dq) `entry_ok` hook (both entry-site params coexist).
- **RESULT (79 markets, 150d, both slips 5.0 + 0.86bps, gates 0.05/0.20/0.40): DURABLE never beats OFF.** Live gate 0.05: durable −14.90 vs off +34.07 (5bps); durable +3.11 vs off +53.57 (0.86bps). Across all 6 gate×slip cells `durable ≤ off`, usually worse by $5–50. The gate REMOVES net-positive entries on Lighter — it concentrates entries into the most-crowded (peak-funding) moments and durable's price P&L is markedly worse. Nothing is both-halves-positive (h1 negative in every row), consistent with the Farmer's known both-halves-negative Lighter verdict.
- **DURABLE ≤ FAILOPEN too** — the restart fail-open is accidentally MITIGATING a gate that is wrong for Lighter. So "recovering" the gate via durable slope history (the Phase-2 code change) would GIVE MONEY BACK (0.05/0.86bps: durable +3.11 vs failopen +24.81).
- **VERDICT: no bot edit.** The Phase-2 hypothesis ("restarts disable a validated edge") is REFUTED — the edge is HL-only and Lighter-NEGATIVE, the exact "backtest on Lighter only" failure the operator rule exists for. ## 2026-07-24 (dp) — the radar's trajectory sensor de-biased: gate the decaying/emerging label on the calibrated slope_t, not the sample-size-biased traj_delta + the audit-backlog triage filed (shadow-only; no real-money change)

- **THE BIAS (found auditing the (cn) radar's own new sensor).** The trajectory gate used `traj_delta = t_recent − t_full` — a HALF-sample t-stat minus a FULL-sample one. Because t scales with √n, that difference is biased NEGATIVE by ~(1/√2 − 1)·t from sample size ALONE, growing with t (Monte-Carlo mean −0.49 at t≈2, −1.53 at t≈6). A same-level book whose recent half is merely NOISIER (lower t, not lower mean) trips it with ZERO real decay: **~15% of constant-effect books read "decaying."** `slope_t` — a calibrated OLS-slope t-stat (~N(0,1) under a constant effect, **−14** on the real Farmer shape) — was already computed but UNUSED.
- **THE FIX.** The decaying/emerging label now gates on `slope_t` (≤ −2.0 / ≥ +2.0, a *significant* trend) with the median/faded corroboration unchanged; `traj_delta` stays a reported diagnostic. Measured false-"decaying" on constant books drops **~15% → ~2%**. The Farmer verdict is unaffected — it was over-determined by the decisive `_faded` ratio + independent thirds + the concentration collapse, never the trajectory gate (see `RADAR_TRAJECTORY_AUDIT_2026-07-23.md`).
- **MUTATION-TESTED, and the fixture DISTINGUISHES the gates.** New selftest 9b: a same-level, noisier-recent book (`traj_delta = −1.22`, `slope_t = 0.0`, recent median −0.5) must read STABLE. Reverting the gate to `traj_delta ≤ −1.0` flips it to "decaying" and the selftest goes RED (verified). Suite now 19 checks; `fleet_radar --selftest` green.
- **HONEST SCOPE.** `fleet_radar` is shadow, publish-only, zero consumers — no real money. The gain is a Monte-Carlo-measured noise-robustness property; a live-Lighter-tape confirmation that it never UNDER-catches a genuine gradual fade remains a follow-up (needs DB). The (cn) deploy-orphan fix and the deploy-coverage CI wiring I also scoped this session were landed independently by the bull change set (already on main) — not re-submitted here.
- **AUDIT-BACKLOG TRIAGE filed** (`AUDIT_BACKLOG_TRIAGE_2026-07-23.md`): the 5 lever-authority findings (live/xp.funding.enter_apr INERT-PINNED = the HL-hourly→Lighter-8h units bug; EXIT_APR/HARD_STOP UNLEVERED = real-money loss-decisive knobs; taker.sl_cooldown_h DARK) and the venue-purity backtest backlog — all real-money-gated or data-starved, verified still current on today's main, routed to the 28-Jul review, none declared in `*_OK` unilaterally.

## 2026-07-23 (cu) — "THEN WIDEN": the evidence says the live funding gate must NOT widen up — measured on Lighter's own tape (operator: "proceed")

- **THE PIVOT FROM BRAKES TO EVIDENCE.** With the brakes in (cq-ct), the real-money widening was gated on ONE thing: a gate that's actually profitable on Lighter's tape. Ran `scripts/backtest_funding_lighter.py --days 180 --universe 25 --refresh` against Lighter's own API (settled hourly fundings + candles, 25 markets, 2026-01-24→07-23) — Lighter-only, per doctrine. Result in `FUNDING_GATE_LIGHTER_2026-07-23.md`.
- **WIDENING THE ENTRY GATE UP LOSES — decisively.** The gate curve: 0.02 +$19.82 (both halves +), 0.05 (LIVE) +$3.57 (both +), then it goes NEGATIVE and stays there — 0.08 −$10.54, 0.12 −$47.14 (both halves −), 0.20 −$28.38 (both −), 0.30 −$24.78 (both −). The premise "the lever needs more space to operate" is, for THIS lever, backwards: more space upward = more loss. The lever-authority audit's "the decisive ~10% apr sits above the 0.075 ceiling" is real, but reaching it is a LOSS — the tight ceiling is PROTECTIVE.
- **THE STRUCTURAL FINDING (bigger than the sweep): the strategy is COST-bound, not gate-bound.** At gate 0.05, carry earned over the 9h median hold = 0.5bps vs a 10bps round-trip slip → **operative breakeven ≈ 97% apr**, and the venue floor is 3.5% / ETH ~8%. 56% of trades exit because the funding signal EVAPORATED (flip+cold) before the carry could out-run slippage. The small positive rows are a few tp winners barely clearing cost — noise around zero, not a durable edge. No gate change fixes a cost structure.
- **CORRECTION to an earlier read.** The audit relayed the live LEDGER as "negative in both halves"; the SIMULATED gate at 0.05 is marginally POSITIVE both halves (+6.79/+1.33). Both are true — the live book is negative from execution + coin concentration (radar `cn`), the gate itself is ~breakeven in idealised fills. The unifying truth is stronger and unchanged: the edge is smaller than the cost, so widening the gate up automates a loss.
- **RECOMMENDATION (operator authority — surfaced, not taken):** do NOT widen `live.funding.enter_apr` up; the tight bound stays. The productive lever is COST (longer holds on genuinely high-funding coins, fewer flips) or idling the live arm — not the gate. `live/xp.funding.enter_apr`'s INERT finding is left OPEN on purpose (the lever-authority guard uses it as a test fixture); the WHY-it's-correct lives in the evidence doc. ## 2026-07-23 (ct) — AUTONOMY BRAKE 4: the live Farmer no longer books PHANTOM closes that corrupt the deciders' data (operator: "fix the brakes, then widen")

- **THE BUG (real-money code).** `venues/lighter_client.market_close()` returns `None` (no exception) when the venue holds NO position under the key — already flat, externally closed, or liquidated between the `positions()` read and the close call. The Ticket Taker guards this everywhere ("None is a FAILED close … leaving position, retry"); the Funding Farmer guarded it NOWHERE. All three close sites (manage-loop `:1377`, blind-stop fail-safe `:1284`, `_flatten_all` `:971`) booked a close on `None` — fabricating `price_pnl` on the STALE `held` size and incrementing `n_closed`/`n_wins`. Those counters feed the promotion judge (`experiment_judge`, the only writer of `live.funding.*`) and the brain's reduce opinion, so a phantom close silently CORRUPTS the very data any autonomous widen/promote decision rests on — a data-integrity brake that had to close before authority widens.
- **THE FIX — mirror the taker, verified not to leak.** Each site now `if _res is None:` logs and skips the booking. Confirmed safe against a meta-leak: the manage loop is keyed on `set(pos) | set(meta)` and pops meta whenever the venue shows `held==0` (`:1256-1259`), so a vanished position's meta is reconciled on the NEXT loop (or the close is retried if it's still held) — we deliberately DON'T pop meta on `None`, matching the taker's conservative "leave it, reconcile/retry" semantics. All three `market_close` sites covered (the 4th hit is a docstring).
- **Restrict-in-effect — it can only ever record FEWER closes, never more, and never a fabricated P&L.** No entry/exit/stop/sizing logic changed. Existing `lighter_funding_bot --selftest` 4/4, real-money + financial suites green, full suite green, born-dark + sdk-pin + venue-purity + deploy-coverage guards green.
- **Honest test gap:** the close path lives inside `run()`'s loop and isn't extracted into a unit, so a dedicated None-close selftest needs a small `run()`-harness refactor of real-money code — deliberately deferred rather than rushed here; the fix mirrors the taker's already-fixture-tested None semantics. **DEPLOY: real-money file — reaches the SHADOW funding twin on the freqtrade-bots auto-deploy; the LIVE Farmer (`trail-blazer-live`, gate0) needs an operator ff/dispatch. Inert-until-then and restrict-only, so no urgency.** This completes brakes 1-5 of "fix the brakes, then widen".

## 2026-07-23 (cs) — AUTONOMY BRAKE 2: the proposal channel is now author-bound — no unauthenticated hand on a real-money release (operator: "fix the brakes, then widen")

- **THE HOLE.** `fleet_proposals.propose()` had NO author binding (unlike `fleet_tuning.write_levers`, which enforces `AUTHOR_LANES`): ANY organ importing the module could propose ANY registered lever, including `live.funding.*`. And the judge's `proposal_fade` treats a fresh RESTRICT proposal on a promoted live lever as an EARLY RELEASE (`experiment_judge.py:954` reads `fprop.fresh_proposals()`), so a buggy or spurious proposal from any author was an unauthenticated trigger that could pull a good, measured-positive promotion off real money before its fade bar. Exactly the surface you do NOT want open before widening authority.
- **THE BRAKE.** New `PROPOSAL_AUTHOR_LANES` + `_author_may_propose()` — the PROPOSE-side twin of `AUTHOR_LANES`, deliberately DISTINCT from it (proposing is evidence-in, so the shadow proposers are broader than the write authors: event-sentinel WRITES only its detection lane but legitimately PROPOSES `taker.*`). A live-lane proposal now requires an explicitly sanctioned author (`impl-shortfall` → `lighter-live`, the only one); an unlisted author may propose only non-live (shadow) lanes, never real money — the same fail-safe shape as fleet_tuning's unbound-author rule. Enforced at BOTH write (`propose`) AND read (`fresh_proposals`), so a live.* proposal that is stale, pre-brake, or DB-poked is filtered before any consumer sees it.
- **NO LEGITIMATE PROPOSER BROKEN — verified against the real callers.** The four live proposers keep working on their actual levers: brain / event-sentinel / respiration → `taker.*` (shadow), impl-shortfall → `live.funding.*` (live). Confirmed by reading every `propose()` call site and its exact `set_by` string, not assumed. New selftest pins the gate both ways (sanctioned live proposal survives; a rogue `live.funding.enter_apr` is dropped at write and filtered on read).
- Shadow/intelligence-layer channel — no real-money code touched, no live behaviour change; the brake can only ever REFUSE a proposal, never enact one. Full suite green, all guards green. Brake 2 of 5 (remaining: brake 4, Farmer phantom-close — the one real-money-file change, saved for last and its own commit).

## 2026-07-23 (ff) — the LIVE daily-loss rails were capital-BLIND: a deposit MASKED a drawdown, a withdrawal FABRICATED a halt — BOTH real-money bots fixed to measure trading P&L NET of capital (operator: "go ahead and deploy")

- **THE DEFECT (live-surface audit, both real-money bots).** The Ticket Taker AND Funding Farmer daily-loss rails compared RAW venue equity to a RAW `day_start` that was never capital-adjusted, while `capital_adjust + CAPITAL_ADJUST_USD` was subtracted for DISPLAY ONLY (`pnl_abs` / `_live_pnl`) — no rail read it. `account_value()` returns the raw venue total, and on an EquityGuard heal/rebase that total INCLUDES a deposit/withdrawal. So on the live $2/day leash vs a deposit-driven ~$67 book: a same-day **deposit MASKS** an equal drawdown (raw equity rises, day_start doesn't → the rail can't fire) and a same-day **withdrawal ≥$2 FABRICATES** a flatten+halt (raw equity falls, day_start doesn't → the rail flattens on the operator's own cash-out). Latent, not theoretical — the book IS deposit-driven (34.648 + 32.22). No breach/halt/kill had ever fired; rails otherwise SOUND.
- **THE FIX — day_start rides the capital move (operator-confirmed NET of deposits/withdrawals).** `_fold_capital_moves()` now RETURNS the net $ folded; the caller shifts `day_start += delta` so a capital move lands in BOTH the equity read and the rail baseline and CANCELS in the rail's `(day_start − equity)` — the leash measures TRADING P&L only. Applied at BOTH taker fold sites (loop-top + loop-bottom persist) and the farmer's loop-top; the shift fires ONLY in the day_start-already-set branch (the None-adoption branch takes `equity`, already capital-inclusive — shifting there would DOUBLE-count). `venues/safety.py` UNTOUCHED (shared by 4 bots). REJECTED the tempting `equity − capital_adjust − CAPITAL_ADJUST_USD` form: that ledger is LIFETIME (vs `live_baseline`) but `day_start` is a DAILY baseline already capital-inclusive — subtracting it would trip the rail every day.
- **TESTS + mutation.** New taker `--selftest-live` **4b (deposit-mask: a +$100 deposit exactly offsets a −$100/−10% loss → the rail MUST still flatten)** and **4c (withdrawal-phantom: −$30 withdrawal, zero trading loss → the rail must NOT fire)**; `_StubVenue` gained `pop_capital_moves` mirroring the guard's pop-once contract. Mutation-verified: neuter the shift (`_fold`→`return 0.0`) and 4b goes RED ("a deposit masked a real drawdown"). The db52724 EquityGuard deposit-heal regression stays **47/47 green** — the fix does not reopen it. The Farmer shares the identical shift but has no main-loop harness (only unit selftests) → compile+logic-verified, not fixtured (a pre-existing coverage gap, stated not hidden). `--selftest`/`--selftest-live` green; full suite green; born-dark + sdk-pin + venue-purity + conflict-marker guards green.
- **THIS IS A REAL-MONEY BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (unlike (fe), which shipped dormant).** The live rails now fire net-of-capital. Restrict-correctness ONLY: it never sizes up, flips `dry_run`, or adds keys — it makes the rail fire when it SHOULD (a deposit-masked drawdown) and NOT when it shouldn't (a phantom on a cash-out). Residual (declared): a capital move landing inside the 60s `confirm_daily_loss` window isn't reflected until the next loop — negligible, fail-OPEN for deposits.

The two LIVE services are on NO auto-path: dispatched via `gh workflow run 305025607 -f services="trail-blazer-live,tide-rider-lighter-live"` (`railway up` from main), then BUILD-STAMP-verified on each running container (never trust the branch label — [[railway-cli-frozen-services]]). gate0 (`claude/lighter-gate0`, the Farmer's deploy branch) fast-forwarded to main so the fix is DURABLE across a Farmer rebuild — it was 8 commits stale (the loaded gun, [[gate0-stale-lacks-tonights-guardrails]]).

- **THE RIGHT GATE IS QUOTED SPREAD, NOT VOLUME — measured, then shipped dormant.** `venue_orders.spread_bps` is recorded at decision time (179/179 shadow rows) = a true at-open observable, historically present → BACKTESTABLE on the ledger. Quoted spread PREDICTS realised slippage and it HOLDS EX-BOT (pearson r=+0.44 all / **+0.42 ex-BOT**; per-fill: STRC 98→46, IWM 45→27, NBIS 37→45, **SOXL 24→78**). The gate `spread ≤ ~20bps` is the ONLY gate (spread OR volume) that improves BOTH halves EX-BOT while excluding ONLY losers (ex-BOT keep 46, cum +$14.15 vs +$8.96, **t=+1.30**, dH1 +2.18/dH2 +3.01, excl $0 win/−$5.19 loss). The VOLUME floor DIV_VOL_M was RE-REJECTED at grown n (its "+$13.57 t=1.83 both-halves" was a BOT mark-pathology artifact — BOT 47/99 closes, vol_m 0.12-0.59 but 747bps slip, already vetoed; ex-BOT every volume floor FAILS both-halves; volume≠toxicity: 1000BONK 0.12M/4.8bps/+$5.84 wrongly cut while SOXL kept).
- **`TT_SPREAD_GATE_BPS`, ONE knob, THREE modes, DEFAULT 0 = FULLY DORMANT** (no book fetch, zero new network calls, byte-for-byte prior behaviour). A HIGH value (e.g. 9999) = RECORD-ONLY (fetch + log the decision-time spread on LIVE fills — closing the live-spread telemetry gap, blocking nothing); a moderate value (e.g. 20) = ACTIVE gate. The book is fetched ONLY when enabled and ONLY for a candidate that cleared every cheap filter (≤MAX_OPEN fetches/cycle). Fail-OPEN (a missing/empty book NEVER blocks — same contract as the coin-quality veto); RESTRICT-ONLY (an over-wide spread only ever SKIPs). `book_spread_bps` mirrors the ShadowBroker's fill-time math exactly, so the gate reads the same number the ledger records.

The tape-replay harness is BLIND to spread ('lighter-market' snapshots carry marks only) — the gate is FILL-LEDGER-validated, not tape-replayed, and that limitation is what the live-spread telemetry exists to close. Not every ex-BOT loss is execution: NBIS (−$6.36, ~10bps slip) is DIRECTIONAL (long-divergence wrong in a downtrend), which no liquidity gate fixes.
- **Evidence + tests.** `scripts/study_taker_spread_gate.py` reproduces the table (spread→slip ex-BOT + the gate sweep, FULL and EX-BOT). ## 2026-07-22 (cc) — the fill read fires BEFORE the trade is on the tape: the venue told us how long to wait and the repo had ZERO references to it

- **THE BLOCKER UNDER EVERY IDENTITY TIER, and it was never identity.** 0 of 81 live orders have EVER produced a measured fill. Three sessions rebuilt the naming — client_order_index, then (br)'s tx_hash — and the symptom never moved: both tiers report `no-match:both`, i.e. **both tapes WERE read and our trade was not on them**. No naming scheme fixes a tape that does not contain the trade yet. There is no wait anywhere on either live bot's order path: `read_fill` fires the instant the order is submitted and retries up to SIX tape reads back-to-back, all inside the window the venue itself says the transaction needs.
- **The venue hands us that window on every order and nobody read it.** `RespSendTx.predicted_execution_time_ms` is returned to the caller and stashed at `venues/lighter_client.py:628`/`:826`; `grep -rn predicted_execution` over the whole repo returned **0 hits**.
- **The fix, additive end to end:** `venues/fills.py` gains `read_fill(..., settle_ms=None)` — a post-submission wait driven by the venue's own estimate, clamped by `SETTLE_CAP_MS` (env `FILL_SETTLE_CAP_MS`, default 2500ms) so a zero/absent/garbage value can never stall a trading loop. It delays the MEASUREMENT, never the order (the order is already sent), and `settle_ms=None` reproduces the pre-22-Jul behaviour exactly, so every existing caller and fixture is untouched. `venues/lighter_client.py` gains `_settle_ms_of(resp)` — probed across response shapes exactly like `_tx_hash_of`, because a None here costs only the wait, never an error — threaded into BOTH order return paths. Both live bots pass it through: 8 sites in `lighter_funding_bot.py` (2 signatures, 2 read_fill calls, 4 call sites), 4 in `lighter_ticket_taker.py`.
- **MEASUREMENT ONLY, per this file's own rule:** nothing here may block, delay or unwind an order. The wait is after submission, bounded, and wrapped so a bad value degrades to no wait.
- **Two real breaks caught while writing it, both worth recording.** (1) `ast.parse` reported my first edit as valid while `py_compile` correctly rejected it — `from __future__ import annotations` had ended up after the new imports. **`ast.parse` is not a compile check.** (2) `settle_ms` was referenced in the body one edit before it existed in the signature. Both caught by compiling rather than trusting.

## 2026-07-22 (ca) — 🎫 the taker joins the coin-quality veto: the fleet's one automated actuator had ONE consumer, and the other book was bleeding 747bps into a lens the brain still grades POSITIVE

- **The third instance of "a kill switch must reach the CONSUMER."** `market_context` publishes `coin-vetoes` (measured slippage > 15bps over >=5 orders/14d) and it was the fleet's single automated restrict-only actuator — but its ONLY reader was `lighter_funding_bot.py:1033`. - **What it cost, measured:** BOT/USDC carries **747.6 bps mean |slippage| over 93 taker orders** (81.9bps spread) — the next-worst book it trades is SOXL at 20.9, i.e. ~36x. On 22-Jul the taker put **44 of its 52 closes** through BOT and the `short-divergence` realised mean fell to **-0.695%/trade**, dragging the all-time lens to -0.310% over n=70 with both halves negative. **The lens did not decay.** The brain's counterfactual grade of the divergence SIGNAL is unchanged and positive — `ehit4h 0.536 [0.516,0.557]` at n=10522 — because it grades tickets, not slipped fills. One un-vetoed illiquid book was eating a working lens, and the realised-vs-graded gap was the only visible symptom.

Contract transcribed VERBATIM from the Farmer's so the two cannot drift: RESTRICT-ONLY (exits, held positions and stops untouched), fail-OPEN on a missing OR STALE payload (a fossil veto set is not evidence; a market-context that died empty must not silently disable the veto forever), never raises into the loop. Symbol form is normalised (`BOT` vs `BOT/USDC`) because matching one form only would have made the guard silently inert — precisely the failure class it exists to fix.
- **Verified against LIVE data, not just the selftest** (the taker's `--selftest` skips much of the entry path — mutation-test the suite that RUNS the code): payload fresh at 109s/3600s ttl, veto set {ADA, BOT, SOXL}, both symbol forms blocked, non-vetoed and null symbols allowed, stale payload vetoes nothing, and against the scout's CURRENT 20 tickets it blocks exactly one — `divergence BOT`. Full taker selftest green; born-dark + venue-purity guards green.
- **[CORRECTED, same day, by an 8-agent adversarial review]** the close-leg hypothesis below is **REFUTED**: `venues/fills.py:107` emits the `tx-miss:` token ONLY inside `if tx_hash:`, so a truthy hash DID reach both tapes; `market_close` returns the hash by identical construction to `market_open` (`lighter_client.py:828` vs `:635`); and "both were close legs" is SELECTION — there have been ZERO live open legs since the fix deployed. Historically closes match *better* (4/22 vs 1/17). **The real blocker is upstream of every identity tier:** the fill read is issued with ZERO wait, and `RespSendTx.predicted_execution_time_ms` — returned to the caller and stashed at `lighter_client.py:628`/`:826` — has **0 references anywhere in the repo**. No naming scheme fixes a tape that does not yet contain the fill.

- **🚫 Time-stop study (the (bx) second lane) — DO NOT ENACT, the budget-saturation question closes:** `scripts/study_family_time_stop.py` (harness cross-validates against the accepted breakout study to the cent; 4h 500d + 1d 499d Lighter tape, both regimes). ## 2026-07-18 (aq) — the (ao) deposit-heal couldn't fire on the RUN-ONCE bot; the reject streak now survives the relaunch (hardened across 4 adversarial findings)

- **THE OTHER HALF OF THE (ao) INCIDENT — measured on the deploy that shipped (ao).** (ao) heals a deposit-stuck bot by re-baselining after `rebase_after` consecutive continuity rejects. It healed the Funding Farmer within minutes — but the Ticket Taker stayed at `equity=None` after the same deploy. Root cause: the Farmer is a long-lived `while True` process, so its EquityGuard (and the in-memory reject streak `self._rejects`) persists across reads; the Ticket Taker is **RUN-ONCE** (`tickettaker_loop.sh`: `python3 lighter_ticket_taker.py; sleep 300`), so every 300s a fresh process rebuilds the guard and `self._rejects` resets to `[]`. The streak could never reach `rebase_after`, so the rebase **never fired** — a deposit strands any run-once bot equity-blind forever (which ALSO disables the daily-loss rail, since it needs a non-None equity).
- **THE FIX — persist the reject streak, but ONLY for run-once bots, and only via the corroborated path.** The persisted blob is now `{"last": <accepted>, "rejects": [...]}` for a run-once bot; a fresh process restores the streak, appends its own reject, and rebases once the PERSISTED streak reaches `rebase_after`. Every `_judge` verdict is unchanged.
- **HARDENED ACROSS 3 ADVERSARIAL FINDINGS (parallel refutation before deploy), each a real hole closed before shipping:**
  1. **Funding-bot regression (HIGH).** Persisting the streak unconditionally strips the long-lived Farmer's redeploy "streak reset": a dislocation active across a `railway up` would restore a 2-long streak, skip the boot double-read (`has_state=True`), and its first read becomes reject #3 → rebase onto the phantom via the un-corroborated `total_stable` path. **Fix:** persistence is OPT-IN (`persist_reject_streak`, `EquityGuard`/`LighterClient`) — the Ticket Taker sets it, the Farmer leaves it False and behaves EXACTLY as before (memory-only streak, flat blob, redeploy reset intact).
  2. **`mark_gap`→`continuity` laundering (HIGH).** `need` is sized by the current read's reason, but `recent` pulled the last `need` persisted rejects of ANY reason — so two high-bar `mark_gap` rejects (need=12) + one fresh `continuity` read (need=3) rebased at the low bar via `total_stable`, onto the exact 2026-07-11 phantom class. **Fix:** the streak RESETS on a reason change (a streak is "N consecutive SELF-CONSISTENT rejects"), and on the run-once path `total_stable` is disabled entirely — a run-once bot heals ONLY via the fully-corroborated `coll_stable`; a total-only phantom keeps it equity-blind (recoverable) instead of rebasing.
  3. **Heal-failure if `collateral` included uPnL (conditional).** `coll_stable`'s `identity_ok` (`total == collateral + Σupnl`) is only satisfiable if the venue's `collateral` field excludes unrealized P&L. **Resolved by measurement, not assumption:** queried the live Lighter account (733196) — `collateral − (total − Σupnl) = 1e-6`, i.e. **collateral EXCLUDES uPnL**; the identity holds and the deposit genuinely heals via `coll_stable`. Confirms the (ao) design's core premise on the real venue.
  4. **Legacy-blob entries bypass (HIGH/CRITICAL — the second verification round's DEPLOY BLOCKER, reproduced end-to-end).** The live Taker's first post-deploy blob is the OLD flat shape with no `entries`, so (ao)'s `entries_match` graceful-degradation skipped entry verification outright — and an entry+upnl lockstep phantom (entry 100→70, upnl +30, gap held at 0) then **false-rebased +13%** into the daily-loss rail via `coll_stable`, on the exact state the deploy ships into. **Fix — the collateral-moved discriminator:** when entry verification is impossible (no stored entries), the rebase additionally requires `|collateral − baseline collateral| > tol`. A genuine deposit MOVES ledger cash; the lockstep phantom keeps collateral flat (its injection rides upnl, and `identity_ok` pins total = collateral + upnl). Honest legacy-blob deposit → heals; phantom → stays equity-blind (recoverable). The verified-wrong naive fix (just disabling the degradation on the persist path) is documented in-code as a DO-NOT: it re-strands the honest deposit — the exact incident this file heals.
- **Streak hygiene:** restore keeps only a CONTIGUOUS, SAME-REASON run (each reject within `_REJECT_STREAK_MAX_GAP_S=900s` — 3× the run-once cadence — of its successor, newest recent vs now), so a dead sub-`need` episode can't be stitched to a fresh reject a relaunch later; future-stamped rejects (clock skew / corrupt blob) are dropped rather than allowed to anchor the walk. In-memory streak bounded to `4*rebase_after`. Old flat blobs read as last-only (backward-compatible).
- Tests (+14, 37 in the guard file): run-once relaunch heals a drifting-book deposit ACROSS process boundaries (via `coll_stable`); long-lived guard NEVER persists a streak (Farmer regression guard); `mark_gap`→`continuity` is not laundered; a bare `total_stable` phantom without corroboration is refused on the run-once path; **the legacy-blob PAIR — lockstep phantom rejects AND honest deposit heals on the same no-entries state**; the persist-flag wiring pinned at all three sites (EquityGuard default False / LighterClient threads it / Taker opts in, venue_context does not); future-ts junk dropped; reason-change resets; wide-gap and stale streaks drop; accept clears the streak. Full suite **161 passed, 1 skipped**; `sim_equity_guard` 0/32 dislocated prints accepted / 0% false rejects; both live bots' selftests + born-dark/venue-purity/sdk-pin guards green.
- **Declared follow-up (pre-existing, both live bots, NOT worsened here):** `day_start_equity` never re-baselines on a detected mid-day cash move — a withdrawal can trip the daily-loss rail as if it were a trading loss, a deposit loosens it (`lighter_ticket_taker.py` day-start adoption; mirror in the funding bot). Verified MEDIUM / non-blocking; agenda for the Jul-21 review.

## 2026-07-18 (ao) — a live deposit stuck BOTH real-money bots at equity=None; the EquityGuard now heals it, hardened across 5 adversarial rounds

- **THE INCIDENT (measured live).** An operator deposit into the Funding Farmer + Ticket Taker sub-accounts stuck both at `equity=None` on the dashboard while still trading. `account_value()` runs each read through the EquityGuard; a deposit is an equity jump the order book can't explain, so the continuity check rejects it — and the self-heal rebase never fires because it compares raw TOTALS, which drift with mids on a small volatile book, so the reject streak is never "consistent". The bot stays equity-blind, which ALSO disables the daily-loss rail (it needs a non-None equity) — the stuck state is itself a real-money hazard.
- **THE FIX (in `_reject`, the self-heal path; `_judge`'s dislocation checks are unchanged).** Rebase when COLLATERAL (the ledger cash figure, which does NOT drift with mids) has been stable across `rebase_after` consecutive continuity rejects, gated so the rebased equity is fully book-corroborated: `identity_ok` (total == collateral + Σupnl), `marks_corroborated` (EVERY held coin's mid readable, so STEP 1 cross-checked every upnl), and `entries_match` (each held position's entry == the entry stored at the last accepted read). Sizes are already pinned by `_same_book`. So every venue-reported per-position value is anchored to a trusted reference; the only residual is O(~2·tol) slack + a persistent collateral corruption — the SAME tradeoff the original total-stable rebase already makes.
- **HARDENED ACROSS 5 ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION ROUNDS**, each of which found a real hole I closed before shipping: (1) an immediate mark-verified accept in `_judge` re-opened the dislocation hole (total is derived from collateral, so a phantom collateral drop co-moves total) → reverted for the rebase approach; (2) a dark book let a phantom upnl rebase → require mark coverage; (3) a tiny dark leg's phantom upnl is unbounded by its notional → require EVERY coin's mid; (4) a compensating upnl+entry corruption kept STEP 1's gap at 0 → require `entries_match`; (5) the state-restore path rebuilt `_last` WITHOUT entries, which would have re-stranded the currently-stuck bots on the very deploy that ships the fix → restore entries + degrade `entries_match` gracefully for legacy snapshots.
- **KNOWN RESIDUAL, declared:** a same-coin-size close+reopen with a venue-stale entry can bypass `entries_match` (MEDIUM) — NOT exploitable for these bots, which size by USD clip (equal coin-size ⇒ equal price ⇒ equal entry); fully closing it needs fill/nonce tracking, disproportionate to a non-exploitable edge. The bounded ~2·tol over/under-statement is the irreducible floor of any tolerance check.
- Tests: deposit heals via collateral-stable rebase on a drifting book; transient collateral glitch, dark book, partial-dark leg, entry-corruption phantom all still reject; legacy-restore (no entries) still heals. 24 equity-guard tests, full suite 148 green. `venues/` selftests + all deploy guards green.

## 2026-07-18 (al) — the history charts are interactive now — hover a crosshair to read value + time, and it survives the live-morph

- **THE TENSION I CREATED, RESOLVED.** Two commits ago I made "these pages carry NO inline `<script>`" the REASON the live-morph is safe (innerHTML swap doesn't re-run scripts, so a JS-drawn chart would die on the first data update). An interactive chart needs JS — so a naive `onmouseover` per chart would break the moment the page morphed. Solved with EVENT DELEGATION: one `pointermove` handler on `document`, attached once OUTSIDE `#station`, so it survives every morph and simply re-targets whatever `.ichart` SVGs the fresh markup contains. No per-chart init to die.
- **NEAR-ZERO DATA COST.** The 9 equity/P&L curves were already server-rendered `<polyline>`s — the shape is ALREADY in the DOM. So the handler reads the polyline's own points for geometry and inverts a tiny 5-number scale per chart (`data-lo/hi` map y→value, `data-t0/t1` map index→time). Nothing per-point is embedded; the page grew by ~5 attributes per chart, not 9×420 points.
- **HTML overlay, not SVG.** The charts use `preserveAspectRatio="none"` (they stretch to full width), which would distort any SVG `<text>`. So the crosshair, the dot on the curve, and the tooltip are position:fixed HTML overlays the handler creates once and repositions — crisp at any width. Value formatted like `money()` (`+1,234.56`), time in UTC to match the page.
- **VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER, including the hard part.** Hovered a chart → correct readout ("+29.65 · 2026-07-15 16:39 UTC"), crosshair + dot + tooltip visible (screenshot). Then the make-or-break test: I reproduced the poller's morph EXACTLY (fetch page, swap `#station.innerHTML`), which DESTROYS the chart node — confirmed `chart_node_replaced: true` — and hover on the FRESH node STILL produced a correct tooltip. A per-chart init would have been dead there; delegation isn't. `node --check` on the combined JS; 9 charts render with valid scale attrs against the live DB. Guards green.
- **FOR THE NEXT PERSON:** the delegated handler keys on `.ichart` + the 5 data-attrs and reads a `<polyline>`. Any new chart that follows that shape is interactive for free. The morph-safety rule still stands for anything ELSE that needs JS — delegate from document, or live outside `#station`.

## 2026-07-18 (ak) — the live-station treatment now covers every dashboard page, applied once at the router

- **FOLLOW-ON to the main-page live station.** The five drill-down pages (/vitals health, /history, /learning, /periods, /market) still used full-page `<meta refresh>` (60–300s). They now live-update in place with the same heartbeat + morph, so the whole console is one operating station, not one live page and five reprinted photos.
- **DONE MECHANICALLY, not by hand-surgery.** A single `live_wrap(page)` helper transforms any page string: `<meta refresh>` → `<noscript>` fallback, inject heartbeat CSS, wrap the body in `<div id="station">` (morph target) closing before the footer so the footer + poller stay OUTSIDE it, drop the heartbeat in the footer + poller before `</body>`. Applied at the ONE dispatch site in do_GET (`live_wrap(render_vitals())` …), so every route gets identical treatment and none can be forgotten. Idempotent — it no-ops on the main page, which is already wired inline.
- **SAFE on these pages SPECIFICALLY because they carry NO inline `<script>`.** A morph replaces innerHTML and does not re-run scripts, so a page that drew a chart in JS would break after an update. Verified 0 `<script>`/`<canvas>` across all five before wiring; they render everything server-side. If a future drill-down adds a content script, it must re-init after morph or opt out of `live_wrap`.
- **VERIFIED:** `live_wrap` unit-tested (11 structural checks + idempotency + a footer-less edge case); all five pages rendered against the live DB and re-checked (DOM-balanced #station, noscript fallback, heartbeat present, poller outside the morph target); and the SERVED /vitals fetched through the real HTTP path confirmed correct. The client JS is byte-identical to the main page's, already browser-proven (in-place morph with a surviving sentinel, age ticker, red-OFFLINE on server loss). Guards green: deploy-coverage 0-orphan, born-dark 20/20.

## 2026-07-18 (aj) — the dashboard is now a live operating station: every item updates in place, no reload, and it shows when it goes blind

- **THE PROBLEM.** The whole dashboard refreshed by full-page `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` — 30s on the main page, up to 5 min elsewhere. That reloads the entire document: it flickers, drops your scroll position, and between reloads the page is a frozen snapshot with no indication of how old it is. Not an operating station — a periodically-reprinted photo.
- **THE FIX — in-place morph, gated by a cheap change signal.** New `/tick.json` (public, no auth — it is one timestamp) returns `GREATEST(max(bot_pnl.updated_at), max(bot_state.updated_at))` in ONE query. A vanilla-JS layer polls it every 5s and, ONLY when the version moves, fetches the page and swaps the `#station` container's innerHTML. Every card, total and organ updates at once; nothing flickers; scroll is kept. Because the expensive full render runs only when data actually changed, DB load is at or below the old blanket 30s meta-refresh, not above it.
- **IT SHOWS WHEN IT IS BLIND.** A heartbeat dot in the footer reads live (green) / reconnecting (amber) / **OFFLINE (red)** with a 1-second "updated Ns ago" ticker. An operating station must never present stale data as current — if the poller loses the server, the operator sees red within ~10s instead of numbers that quietly stopped moving.
- **FAIL-SAFE, THREE WAYS.** (1) `<noscript><meta refresh></noscript>` — a JS-off browser still refreshes. (2) The poller lives OUTSIDE `#station`, and innerHTML assignment does not run `<script>` tags, so a morph can never kill the loop driving it. (3) If `/tick.json` stays unreachable past the fallback window the page force-reloads — a broken poller degrades to the OLD behaviour, never a frozen screen. The admin "Manage bots" panel is deliberately OUTSIDE the morph target so its forms aren't swapped mid-interaction.
- **VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER, not by inspection.** Rendered against the live DB; drove the client with a mutating harness. Confirmed: green heartbeat + the morph token advancing (#22->#23) while an injected sentinel variable SURVIVED (proves in-place, no reload); the age ticker incrementing; and after killing the server, the heartbeat flipping to red "OFFLINE" with the age climbing. `node --check` on the extracted JS; `/tick.json` latency measured (sub-ms on Railway internal net; the 40s local full-render is 26 DB connects x proxy latency from my laptop, unchanged from today and fast on-box). Guards green: deploy-coverage 0-orphan, born-dark 20/20.
- **NOTE:** the code shipped in the prior commit (d67a91e) whose CHANGELOG write crashed on a regex bug before the entry landed — this is that entry. Scope: main page live now; /vitals + other drill-downs still meta-refresh (same one-line treatment extends to each; /vitals next).
