Pairing them would have moved each control book into a keyed, armed container, leaving a **`TT_VENUE` string** as the only thing between the control arm and real orders — trading a hard safety property for a soft one, to buy telemetry convenience. **Withdrawn.** The authorization rested on my framing, and my framing was wrong.
- **SO DRIFT STAYS POSSIBLE BY DESIGN — and is now HARMLESS instead.** `paired_eval` gained an ARM-DRIFT gate, checked BEFORE arm-skew: skew asks *"is the arm running the candidate?"*, drift asks the prior question *"are these two arms the same experiment at all?"*. Neither is a data-volume problem — **no window makes a drifted comparison valid**, so the judge holds, pages urgent, and does **not** age the candidate toward ABANDONED (it isn't the candidate's fault). Same fail-closed shape as ARM SKEW, for the same reason.
- **Build ids come from the arms' own bytes**, read off the SAME `rows` snapshot the bar is computed from — so the drift check and the numbers it gates can never describe different moments. Import is lazy + guarded: a dark sensor costs the judge nothing (it simply cannot claim drift).
- **Fail-safe toward SILENCE, deliberately.** Unknown is NOT drift — a missing stamp means "an arm hasn't published since the hook shipped", which is the normal state through any rollout **including this one**. A gate that fired on unknown would freeze the promotion queue every deploy. Mutation-tested both directions: disabling the gate (promotes across drifted arms) CAUGHT; firing on unknown (freezes the queue) CAUGHT.

## 2026-07-17 (ad) — the taker's id filter was a CLIFF, not a filter: one venue change from measuring NOTHING

- **THE REGRESSION THE ID INTRODUCED.** `venues/lighter_client.py:624-630` matches the client id HARD — a mismatch `continue`s, with no fall back to the `(is_ask, since_ts)` heuristic. So threading `client_order_index` made the taker's fill read exact on the happy path and **strictly worse than the read it replaced on the unhappy one**: if Lighter ever stops echoing the id back as `ask_client_id`/`bid_client_id`, the taker goes from an approximate read to **`no-match:both` — no read at all**, silently. A measurement upgrade whose failure mode is *less measurement than before* is not an upgrade; it is a cliff with a good day.
- **AND THE ID ROUND TRIP IS UNPROVEN IN PRODUCTION.** The taker's only two live orders (STRC 09:08:21Z, 1000BONK 09:13:30Z) were placed an **hour before** the fill-read code landed (a710401, 10:15Z). **No `venue_orders` row has ever carried `measured`/`fill_src`** — so "the id comes back" is an assumption the fleet has never once observed. The fallback is what makes that assumption cost precision instead of the whole reading.
- **FIXED by sharing the Farmer's read, not copying it** — `venues/fills.py`, the same consolidation as `venues/safety.py::open_notional`. Id first; on a **`no-match` only**, one retry without it, labelled `(id-miss: ...)`. Never on `skipped:budget` / `auth-failed` / `api-error` — those mean the tape was never read, so a retry spends the governor's telemetry reserve to fail identically, against lighter_client's explicit rule that telemetry must never make the next `market_open` queue behind it.
- **WHY NOT IN `_our_fills`, where the filter actually lives — two reasons, both fatal:**
  - **The label would lie.** `last_fill_detail` derives its reason from whether an id was *supplied*, not whether it *matched* (`"trades" if client_id is not None else "trades(approx)"`, :700). A fallback inside `_our_fills` returns a blend still labelled `trades` = exact, and `measured_from_reason` stamps it **True**. The fabrication would sit one layer below every test that could catch it.
  - **It would preempt the better tape.** `last_fill_detail` reads the auth'd `trades` (10 rows) then the public `recentTrades` (100 rows). An id-miss on tape 1 currently escalates to tape 2 **with the id**; a fallback inside `_our_fills` blends on tape 1 and returns, never reaching the wider tape where the exact match is more likely. The correct order is id-on-both-tapes, **then** heuristic-on-both — expressible only *above* `last_fill_detail`.
- **A SECOND DEFECT, found in the same read and worse than the first: `measured` was HARD-CODED TRUE.** `_real_fill` returned `real, True, reason` for **any** price the venue produced, ignoring the reason string that says whether the venue NAMED the fill or guessed it. An id-less read is a 180s same-side VWAP labelled `trades(approx)` — and it would have been recorded as an exact measurement. **A fabrication wearing a `measured: true` stamp is worse than a null**, because a null is honest about itself. Now derived from the venue layer's own label (`measured_from_reason`), so the two cannot drift.
- **THE DRIFT WAS REAL AND ABOUT TO BECOME REACHABLE.** The two copies disagreed on one rule: an **unmeasured** leg with `d != f` — the taker returned None, the Farmer returned the bps. Unreachable while every read was exact-or-nothing (unmeasured meant no price, so `d == f` always held). **`read_fill`'s fallback is exactly what makes it reachable** — an approx read is the first thing in the fleet's history to carry a real price AND `measured=False`. The Farmer's rule would have fed a **-49.99 bps blend** into `implementation_shortfall._fetch_order_slip`, which does an unfiltered `AVG(slippage_bps)` and reads no `measured` flag — one contaminated row is indistinguishable from a clean one in the live-vs-shadow execution verdict. **Unified on the stricter rule** (the taker's): record the blend as `px_fill`, record NO slippage from it.
- **THE TELEMETRY/BEHAVIOUR BOUNDARY — the taker is NOT the Farmer here, and this is the load-bearing difference.** The Farmer's `_real_exit` is pure forensics: the position is already flat when it runs. The taker's **entry** read becomes `meta[sym]["entry"]`, which the **stop and TP hang off** — it decides when real money closes. So the fallback's price reaches the **ledger only**: `entry_px = _fill_px if _meas else mark`. **Behaviour-identical on every path production can reach today** (an exact match still feeds meta the real fill; no-read still feeds it the mark); only the id-miss path is touched, and it yields the mark — which is what it yields today anyway. The blend is probably a better entry estimate than the decision mark; **"probably" is not a bar this bot clears with real money on the book.** The ledger records it, names it, and a later change can promote it on evidence.
- **NOT CONSOLIDATED, deliberately, and the brief's premise was half wrong.** `_real_exit`/`_slip_bps_of` are **not** four-way duplicated: `_slip_bps_of` exists in **two** bots (Farmer + taker), which are exactly the two that publish `slippage_bps`. `lighter_trend_bot`/`lighter_perp_sniper` have a *same-named, different-contract* function — legacy `last_fill`, no id, no `measured`, and **neither file writes a `venue_orders` row at all**. Their read is an exit PRICE for P&L, not execution telemetry. Folding them in would change two more bots' ledgers for no measurement gain. Left alone.
- **MUTATION-TESTED — 6 mutations, each RED on its own assertion:** revert the fallback to the hard filter (px_fill collapses to the decision), restore `measured=True` (a blend stamped as measured), retry on any failure rather than `no-match` (burns the reserve), the Farmer's old slip rule (records the -49.99 blend), **and both directions of the behaviour boundary** — an unmeasured blend reaching `meta['entry']`, and over-correcting so a *measured* fill can't. The `_StubVenue` grew `echo_ids=False` to model the actual failure — Lighter stops echoing ids, tape readable, our id absent — using lighter_client's **real** reason strings, because a paraphrased fixture tests nothing.
- **A NEAR MISS WORTH RECORDING: I mutation-tested the wrong suite first.** All four originals came back "caught" — by the **Farmer's** suite, while the taker's stayed green — because check 12 lives in `_selftest_live()` and `--selftest` never runs it. `M2 (measured=True)` **SURVIVED** and exposed it. Had the Farmer not shared the code, four green mutations would have read as proof. *Same evening, fourth instance of the same shape: the fixture ran, the wiring did not.*
- **Verification:** taker `--selftest` + `--selftest-live` (13 checks), Farmer, replay, shortfall, trend, sniper, carry, safety, lighter_client (as a module) all green; born-dark OK across 20 images **and negative-tested for this exact import shape** (`venues.fills` imported by an image lacking `COPY venues/` → correctly named); venue-purity unchanged (6 pre-existing, none mine); `audit_sdk_pin` green. **Telemetry + ledger only: no change to what any bot sends** — `market_open`/`market_close`/sizing/rails/`meta['entry']` untouched on every reachable path.
- **DOC ROT FOUND EN ROUTE (not fixed here — shared file):** CLAUDE.md still says the born-dark guard is "NOT wired into CI (the PAT lacks workflow scope) ... the standing follow-up". **It was wired in `ce446c7`** and runs on every push/PR. The rule's own postmortem says a control that relies on remembering is the one that already failed — the doc telling the next reader to go do it by hand is that failure mode's second act.

Only WARNING+ ever surfaced — via the handler of last resort — which is exactly why `Unclosed client session` was visible and nothing else was.

The **funding bot printed it on its first boot**; the **taker printed nothing**. Two bots, same venue layer, one answer — the difference was not the banner, it was that one bot could hear its own dependencies. **A diagnostic that cannot be seen is not a diagnostic**, and the only reason the SDK got measured at all is that the *other* bot happened to configure logging.
- **FIXED — `_setup_logging()`, called from `main()`, never at import.** FOUR modules import this file (`lighter_ticket_replay`, `lighter_scout_tuner`, `strategy_incubator`, `fleet_proprioception`) and **none of them configure logging**, so an import-time `basicConfig` would silently seize the root logger for all four inside the shared freqtrade-bots container. Same reason the `TT_VENUE` gate lives inside `main()`. Idempotent (`basicConfig` no-ops when the root has handlers, so a caller keeps its own setup); `_ctx` — the offline test path — is left alone so the selftests' captured stdout stays clean. Level via `TT_LOG_LEVEL`, default INFO.
- **PINNED BOTH WAYS, because this fix has two ways to be wrong:** silent (no handler → the original bug) and invasive (hijacking four importers). Test 13 asserts the venue logger is INFO-enabled after setup, that merely importing adds **no** handler, that the `_ctx` path configures nothing, and that a second call is a no-op. Verified live: all four importers still see **0 root handlers**.
- **AND THE MUTATION CAUGHT ME A THIRD TIME — same trap, three times in one evening.** My fixture called `_setup_logging()` DIRECTLY, so it proved the FUNCTION worked and said nothing about `main()` calling it — and a helper nobody calls **is the original bug**. **M14 (delete the call site) PASSED.** This is verbatim `_bars` in `funding_carry_bot` and `_slip_bps_of`'s `measured` earlier tonight: **test the helper, forget the wiring.** Fixed with the same source-level call-site assertion; M14/M15/M16 now all fail correctly. The pattern is now three-for-three and belongs in the review: *a fixture that constructs its own inputs proves the arithmetic, never the wiring.*
- **Demonstrated, not asserted:** before `_setup_logging`, `venues.lighter`'s `log.info("lighter signer ready ... lighter-sdk 1.1.2")` printed **nothing**; after, it prints — along with `WARNING venues.lighter equity guard REJECT`. That is the bug and the fix in two lines of output.
- **Verification:** 7 selftests + `--selftest-live` (13 checks) green; born-dark OK across 20 images; `audit_sdk_pin` green; all four importers import with 0 root handlers; deployed to the LIVE taker from a clean `origin/main` worktree per (aa), both real positions intact, 0 orders across the restart.

## 2026-07-17 (g) — the fleet could not measure its own execution, and the organ built to do it was reporting DRIFT as slippage (operator: "measure the real fill cost")
- **THE ORGAN WAS LYING, and the number it lied about decides a live bot.** `implementation_shortfall._slip_bps` compared the LIVE arm's **AVERAGE entry price** against the SHADOW arm's **AVERAGE entry price**, per coin, over a **7-day window**. The two arms enter at DIFFERENT MOMENTS at DIFFERENT PRICES — so the difference of their averages measures **price DRIFT**, not execution. No averaging fixes it; the quantity has no execution meaning unless the fills are the same order. Live proof: **HYPE entry_slip −363.2bps beside exit +359.3bps** — a claim the live arm filled 3.6% BETTER than mark — with ETH 197.3 and LIT 326.1, while the organ's own aggregate said **gap −0.237pp / verdict clean**. Read as execution it said the live book bleeds 2-3% a round trip. **WITHDRAWN**; both keys are now always None. `gap_pp` (the paired per-trade read it IS entitled to) is untouched.
- **Its selftest pinned the BUG.** The fixture fed ONE synthetic trade per arm — where "live avg entry vs shadow avg entry" trivially IS the slippage — so it could not fail. Re-pinned to the withdrawal, plus the honest replacement's contract.
- **THE REAL FINDING: the live bot has NEVER recorded a fill price.** All three `lighter_funding_bot.publish_venue_order` calls passed **`px_decision=px, px_fill=px`** — the decision price echoed back — so `slippage_bps` is NULL on all 48 live order rows. The shadow twin (ShadowBroker walks the real book) reports **0.86bps/fill over n=158, spread 1.70bps**. CLAUDE.md has claimed since 15-Jul that the funding bot "records fill prices"; the code never did. The bot HAS the real fill (`venues.lighter_client.last_fill`, the 16-Jul FILL RECON + the `_real_exit` helper feeding `paper_trades`) — it just never handed it to the order ledger. **FIXED**: both live close paths now publish the decision mid and the REAL venue fill separately, with signed per-order slippage.
- **An echoed decision price now records NULL, never 0.0.** `_real_exit` falls back to the decision mid when the venue read fails, so `px_fill == px_decision` means NO reading — recording it as zero slippage is indistinguishable from a perfect fill. That confusion is the entire blind spot. New `_fetch_order_slip` reports `measurable` + `echoed_decision` per arm so "measured 0" and "never recorded" can never be conflated again.
- **WHY IT MATTERS — the whole Funding Farmer verdict hangs on this one unmeasured number.** Driving slip to zero isolates a **+6.18 bps/trade GROSS edge over 1,911 trades, both halves positive** (TP 0.04 / **STOP 0.10→0.03** / hold 72h at gate 0.05 TRUE — the only config that survives; TP 0.06 fails h2 at every slip, STOP 0.10 never passes). Three estimates, 14x apart, **not one of them measured**. The 5bps/fill that produced "no gate has an edge" was an assumption too.

## 2026-07-17 (at) — the incubator breeds on ELEVEN trades: selection moved to the gametes, gates re-denominated in fills (operator: "an egg needs good sperm and good eggs to fertilise to produce good offspring... let's think genes and DNA")
- **The measurement first.** The incubator's own fitness function, run against the real tape (15-Jul 04:27Z → 16-Jul 23:03Z, 42.9h): **11 closed trades, 10 of them the same stop-loss**, closed net −$14.89; breakout 5/5 SL, dip 3/3 SL, momentum 2/2 SL, divergence 1 TP. A ~90-genotype GA — crossover, mutation, elite carry, both-halves champion gates — was searching a landscape made of eleven fills. Every genotype in the population scores NEGATIVE (best −$14.08). The organ's bottleneck was never its genetics; it is that no fitness signal exists yet. Marks only publish since 15-Jul, so the tape is 2.5 days old and cannot be older.
- **The gates were denominated below one fill — and were hours from opening.** At clip $50 / TP +4% / SL −3%, one trade flipping SL→TP swings **$3.50**; `EDGE_MARGIN` was $2.00 and `HALF_MARGIN` $1.00, so a single lucky fill cleared every anti-overfit bar. They looked strict and were not. Worse, `MIN_TAPE_HOURS=48` was the ONLY thing holding the champion gate shut and the tape crossed 48h at **17-Jul 04:27Z (14:27 Sydney) — the same afternoon**; with `PERSIST_CYCLES=3` hourly cycles the organ would have published a "stable" champion backed by ~12 trades by evening. Now: `MIN_CLOSES` (40) gates on **closed trades, checked first** — hours are not evidence, a 200h tape with 11 closes passed the old floor and was still noise — and both margins are denominated in TRADE SWINGS (`INCUBATOR_EDGE_TRADES`/`HALF_TRADES`; an explicit `INCUBATOR_*_MARGIN` env still wins). Verified on the live tape: `TENTATIVE — 11 closed trades < 40 min`.
- **Selection ran at BIRTH, not at the gametes (the operator's actual point).** `assess_champion` is rigorous and was decorative: the breeding elite were `scored[:ELITE_N]` ranked by raw net, with `both_halves_pos` only breaking exact float ties — i.e. never. So the very +$2.35/h1=+$0.01 noise genotype the champion gate REJECTS still bred, and elite feed forward into the next cycle's population (`prior['elite']`), compounding noise across generations. The gate protected the REPORT; nothing protected the GENE POOL. New `select_elite` filters gametes on MEASURABLE (≥`MIN_GT_CLOSES`=12 closes — you cannot select a genotype you cannot measure; same "starving lens earns its grading diet" logic the tuner runs) AND ROBUST (both halves ≥ HALF_MARGIN — the birth gate moved upstream). On the live tape: **0/20 genotypes viable**, and the old net-max winner is now refused as a gamete. Champion and elite are deliberately decoupled — the fittest is still assessed+published so its reason explains WHY, instead of the card going quiet.
- **Ranking on the point estimate IS the winner's curse** — this file's header said exactly that about the champion in July, then ranked the breeding pool on the point estimate anyway. `rank` now sorts on a one-sided 90% **t lower confidence bound** on total net (`net_lcb`; std error of a sum = sd·√n; t table df 1..30 converging to `brain_stats.Z80`, the fleet's existing convention — the normal approximation is far too generous at n≈11). One trade evidences no edge, ever. Replay gains an ADDITIVE per-lens `pnl_usd` (per-trade net $) — the mean alone cannot price uncertainty; no existing field moved.
- **IMB-10 reconciled + finished.** (as) added deferral-proof marked scoring inside `evaluate` concurrently; kept, lifted to a module-level `_marked` mirroring the tuner's. The missing half: the **MAX_HOLD grid still offered 48h/72h alleles on a 42.9h tape** — both unreachable, and the real tape shows ZERO hold-exits, so with 10-of-11 closes being stop-losses "never close anything" was the strongest gradient in the landscape and the grid supplied the allele to express it. New `reachable_genes` drops unreachable holds before selection can reward them (mirrors the tuner's `_skipped_holds`; never strips a grid bare). Verified: `dropped [48.0, 72.0] -> grid [24.0]`.

## 2026-07-16 (ar) — judge residuals: relative fade, per-half floors, landed-write guard + the immune application invariant (operator: "all 4 go today, assume control")
- **Relative + rolling fade bar (`fade_check`).** The promotion bar is RELATIVE (+0.5pp vs live) but the release bar was ABSOLUTE (mean < 0, cumulative since promotion): a lever that cut live from +0.80%/trade to +0.10% destroyed the edge without inverting the sign and could stay on real money forever — and the cumulative mean converges toward its early value, so a LATE fade became mathematically unreachable. Now: both bars run on the ROLLING last FADE_N closes, and a second release path fires when the recent mean falls ≥ MARGIN_PP below the live arm's own PRE-promotion baseline (the paired window's live mean, stamped into state at PROMOTE as `promote_baseline`). Restrict-only: an extra release path can only pull a lever OFF real money. Fail-safe: missing baseline (old promotions / regen restores) → absolute bar only, byte-identical to the historical behaviour.
- **Per-half sample floors (`paired_eval`).** The full-window floors (30/10) said nothing about the halves, so ONE live trade in a half set that half's entire baseline — the doctrine's central noise filter degenerated into a noise amplifier on the exact comparison that moves real money. Each half now requires shadow ≥ min_closes//2 and live ≥ max(3, live_min//2); an even at-floor split still clears, a lopsided one holds with `why="hX under-powered"`. Derives from the same XPJ_* env knobs.
- **A dropped rail write is not an assert (`_asserted`).** `write_levers` returns None when nothing valid survived (unknown lever / out-of-lane / clamp reject / no DB) and every judge call site discarded it: a silently-dropped write left the judge counting days toward promotion on an arm running env defaults, and could stamp phase=promoted + push "PROMOTED to LIVE" while NO live lever was in force. All four sites now verify the write landed: idle-start refuses to start (and a registry-impossible candidate is marked INVALID and skipped, spending no judge slot, instead of retrying forever); running-re-assert failure HOLDS with the same semantics as ARM SKEW (no promote, no ABANDON aging, clock restarts on recovery, one urgent push per episode via sticky `assert_fail_notified`); a failed PROMOTE write stays RUNNING and retries — the promotion IS the write; a failed promoted-phase re-assert warns once (the TTL expiry to env defaults is already the fail-safe, but it must not be silent while the judge reports "promotion in force").
- **Immune application invariant (`application_sickness`).** The organ whose remit is alive-but-sick could see a lever whose VALUE is impossible but not one whose value is IGNORED — the fleet's largest fresh-but-wrong signal. New invariant on the receipt lanes only (xp.funding.*/live.funding.*, where the arms stamp extra.bars from inside apply_levers — unforgeable by a lever-blind image): a lever in force whose consumer closed ≥2 trades since first-seen (+15min loop grace, tracked in the organ's own `app_seen` map — the tuning payload carries no set-time) with ZERO matching receipts → SICK "enacted but not applied" → sick-list + phone. Deliberately NOT a quarantine: quarantining a lever the consumer provably ignores reverts nothing (that IS the sickness) and would feedback-loop on a healthy arm (quarantine → consumer runs defaults → receipts stop matching → sick forever). Fail-safe: zero closes = no evidence; dark ledger/tuning = nothing flagged.
- **Verification:** judge selftest grows to 12 pinned scenarios (all 9 prior unchanged + per-half floors, relative+rolling fade incl. the cumulative-miss case, asserted-write guard); immune selftest pins the invariant (first-sighting starts the clock, receiptless→sick, matching→healthy, wrong-value receipts→sick — the deaf-arm signature, floor, grace, non-receipt lanes never judged, expired levers forgotten). fleet_tuning + fleet_regen selftests green (payload shape additive).

## 2026-07-16 (aq) — the XP judge was grading an arm that cannot hear it: fail-closed on ARM SKEW (operator: "continue fixes")
- **The defect, on the one path that writes REAL MONEY.** `experiment_judge` was asserting `xp.funding.enter_apr=0.30` at a shadow arm with **no lever-reading code at all** — verified on the running service: `funding-farmer-shadow` → `apply_levers 0 · fleet_tuning 0 · get_lever 0`, and `fleet_tuning.py` → *No such file or directory*. Its gate is `ENTER_APR = os.environ.get("FUNDING_ENTER_APR", "0.40")` with the env **unset**, so it runs **0.40 — the same value the live arm runs**. The paired bar was therefore scoring 07-11-code-at-0.40 against 07-16-code-at-0.40 and attributing the residual (version skew + mark-vs-real fills) to a candidate that was never applied. A PROMOTE writes `live.funding.*`, which the live arm DOES consume. Ledger proof: `perps-funding-lighter-lshadow` = **30 closes, 0 receipts**.
- **Nothing was promoted** (`promoted_ts` null; floors at shadow 1/30, live 0/10) — a live defect caught before it cost anything, not a loss. The incubator had **6 more candidates queued** onto the same arm, each worth a 7–14d judge slot.
- **The missing invariant: nothing verified enactment→APPLICATION.** Every gate validated the DECISION to write a lever (registry clamp, lane binding, AUTHOR_LANES, TTL, paired bar, proprioception episodes); not one validated that a bot ever READ it. `blind_cycles` only catches a DARK ledger ("I can't see the data"), never a lying one ("the rows I see don't reflect my experiment") — precisely the alive-but-sick class `fleet_immune` exists for, which the judge sits outside.
- **The receipt already existed and had ZERO readers.** `lighter_funding_bot.py:493` stamps `extra={"bars": dict(_ACTIVE_BARS)}`, and `_ACTIVE_BARS` is populated **only inside `apply_levers()`** — a lever-blind image structurally *cannot* forge it, which makes a missing receipt **disproof, not silence**. `experiment_judge.py:22` has claimed *"Every close row carries extra.bars"* since 15-Jul; it was never wired. `fetch_paper_trades` never even SELECTed the column.
- **Fix (restrict-only — the gate can only ever BLOCK a promotion, never enable one):** `bot_pnl_store.fetch_paper_trades` now selects `extra` and passes it through (additive; `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS extra JSONB` runs in the same function before the SELECT, so all 7 consumers stay safe). New `ran_candidate(row, levers)` proof predicate. `paired_eval(cand_levers=…)` counts a SHADOW close only when its receipt matches the candidate — the **LIVE arm is deliberately NOT gated**: it is the control running env defaults and only 1 of its 14 rows carries a stamp, so gating it would starve the baseline and freeze the pipeline for good.
- **ARM SKEW is a distinct state, not a false negative.** Closes in-window but zero attributed → HOLD + one urgent push, and explicitly do NOT age toward `ABANDONED` (which would permanently retire a possibly-good candidate on a verdict about an experiment that never ran — `enter-gate-0.30` is the 11-Jul review's own item). On recovery the clock RESTARTS, so days accrued while deaf can't instantly trip `MAX_DAYS`. A stuck, loud queue beats a phantom promotion.

## 2026-07-16 (aa) — AUDIT FIXES: a CRITICAL real-money notional-cap breach + 5 more (two parallel adversarial code reviews of the 15-Jul organs)
Two subagents ran a correctness bug-scan + an integration-synchronicity check over everything built 15-Jul. Synchronicity came back CLEAN (21 levers, one author each, no collisions, no dead reads, deploy wiring complete, immune-quarantine loop correct). The bug-scan found one critical defect and five lesser ones — all fixed here.
- **CRITICAL — live notional-cap breach (`lighter_funding_bot.py`, `lighter_trend_bot.py`).** The entry gate estimated open exposure as `open_now * order_usd` — correct only when every position was opened at the CURRENT clip. The 15-Jul live growth-rail made the clip variable: a `live.clip_scale` DOWN-scale (0.75) shrinks `order_usd`, which RAISES `max_open=floor(cap/clip)`, and with held positions still sized at the larger clip the understated estimate let a new entry breach the operator's hard notional cap (worked example: cap $150, 5×$30 held = at cap, down-scale → a 6th $22.50 entry allowed → $172.50, 15% over; up-then-down reaches ~2×). Ironically triggered by the risk-OFF down-scale, and it contradicted the "cannot add exposure" claim made when the live lane shipped. **Fix:** new `_open_notional()` measures REAL deployed notional — each held position at its OWN clip (`meta['clip']`, or `size*entry` fallback) + this loop's opens at the current clip. Unit-tested against the exact breach scenario on both bots (now correctly blocks the 6th).
- **MEDIUM — `pnl_pct` on the wrong clip (`lighter_funding_bot.py`).** `pnl_pct = pnl / order_usd` used the CLOSE-time clip; a position opened at $30 and closed after an up-scale to $37.50 reported per-trade return understated ~20% — and only the LIVE arm scales, so it skewed the shadow→live promotion judge (and the shortfall tracker). **Fix:** the entry clip is now stamped in `meta['clip']` and passed to `_record_close` at all close sites (both bots).
- **LOW ×3:** (`fleet_regen.py`) `is_clean` reused `immune.organ_invariants`, which freshness-gates — so an AGED history snapshot's corrupt content was never inspected, defanging tier-2 self-repair in its own 3–24h window; now it stamps a fresh `updated` for the content probe (tested: aged `phase=haywire` now detected). (`evidence_board.py`) the live UP-scale gate fail-OPENED on a missing `fleet_dd_7d`; now fails CLOSED (real-money default). (`bot_pnl_store.py`) `fetch_bot_pnl` omitted `pnl_pct`, so the immune organ's NaN/absurd-`pnl_pct` sickness check silently never fired on real rows; column added.
- **ACKNOWLEDGED, not fixed (LOW):** the immune `fleet-alerts` prune races `market_context`'s append; harm is a dropped fresh alert that re-fires next cycle (no data loss, both writers use the identical shape). Left as-is with its owning comment — a proper atomic-append fix exceeds the harm. Also low/by-design from the sync audit: `evidence-review` is operator/scheduler-authored (no in-repo writer); `-lshadow` Dockerfiles omit `fleet_tuning.py` (safe — live-only gate; a footgun ONLY if a shadow were promoted to live without adding the COPY).
Ships main → gate0 ff (both live bots changed — live restart round).

Cheap funding prefilter → candle-scan top 15 (cached ~50min) → book-probe only top 5, sized to the ~21 weight/min governor (Railway ws is CDN-blocked so every book = 1 token). Every entry logs scan evidence to `venue_orders`. Shipped core == backtested core (same veto/score/lookbacks). Adversarially reviewed (4-lens workflow, findings verified): 3 confirmed fixes — the live features were computed on the in-progress forming hourly bar (now dropped → closed-bar only, matching the backtest + no look-ahead); the feature cache is now keyed on the last CLOSED hour (a fresh vol spike is picked up next loop, not ~50min later); the top-15 prefilter divergence documented + env-tunable — plus 2 hardening (defensive best-first book sort for the Railway REST-fallback; scan wrapped so a bug can't crash stop-management). - **Both-perp (self-custody) Yield Harvester hedge — BACKTESTED and REJECTED, not built.** Asked to take the delta-neutral Yield Harvester (`perps-funding-carry`) live on Lighter; it can't (perp-only venue has no same-coin hedge — the code hard-refuses a naked-perp funded run). Chosen self-custody alternative: hedge a hot alt's funding leg with a beta-weighted ETH/BTC perp. `scripts/backtest_carry_hedged.py` (150d real HL funding+price, reuses `.dirfund_cache.json`) compares directional vs major-hedge vs ideal spot-hedge on IDENTICAL signals. HONEST RESULT: the hedge is WORSE than the directional Funding Farmer it was meant to improve (+$5.5 β·ETH vs +$7.9 directional per $25 clip/150d). Structural, not tuning: the funding-receiving side's price P&L is already ~flat (little market-beta to strip), so the hedge mostly adds double slippage + its own funding drag, while the idiosyncratic alt risk it CAN'T hedge is the part that matters; higher gates go negative. - **live trade logging**: the live (lighter_live) order path now records every real open to venue_orders and every real close to venue_orders + paper_trades (venue='lighter', shadow=false, realized P&L, raw exchange response) — so the Lighter Live dashboard card shows trade history, win/loss and per-trade P&L exactly like the paper bots (previously only equity-based total P&L). Ledger writes are guarded separately so they can never mask an order failure. Also fixes a latent bug: live opens now set entry_ts (the 72h time-stop was inert on the live path). Applied to hyperliquid_momo_bot.py (Trail Blazer).
- **live bots no longer die silently (the 'stale' bug)**: when a lighter_live/testnet bot fails venue init (e.g. "private key does not match the one on Lighter"), venue_context now publishes an explicit status=error row with the reason before re-raising — so the dashboard card shows WHY the bot is down instead of just ageing into a stale flag. NEW `scripts/lighter_test_trade.py`: user-run order-path test — default places a POST-ONLY limit 50% below market (cannot fill) then cancels it (sign→submit→cancel proven, ~$0); `--fill` does a real ~$10 market round-trip.
- **live P&L measured from starting collateral, not the $1000 paper baseline** — a live Lighter bot funds from real collateral (e.g. $65), so the dashboard was showing an untraded live account as -$935 (equity - $1000). Fix: the live path records its starting equity once (persisted in bot_state `<bot>-lighter:live`) and publishes pnl_abs = equity - baseline (→ $0 until the first trade); the dashboard also never applies the $1000 paper baseline to `is_live_bot` rows. Applied to momo + perps bots.
- **venues/lighter_client.py — ws hardening**: Lighter's CDN 400s the order-book WebSocket upgrade from cloud (datacenter) IPs though its REST works from the same host, so the live bot spammed reconnect warnings. Now the ws presents a browser-like handshake (Origin + Chrome UA) as a best-effort, and after 3 quick retries goes QUIET (retries every 10 min, logs once) — orderbook() falls back to governed REST snapshots, which work fine for order placement. No functional impact either way.
- **Dockerfile.perpslive**: dedicated image for the bounce-catcher-live Lighter service (hyperliquid_perps_bot.py; same inert-until-disarmed pattern as Dockerfile.momolive).
- **dashboard: dedicated "⚡ Lighter Live" section** — real-money `<bot>-lighter` rows are pulled out of the paper grid into their own bordered, red-accented section at the top of the page (header shows live equity · P&L · bot count + a REAL MONEY tag), so live money is never lost among the paper cards. Render-tested. `perps-donchian-breakout-lighter` went live this session ($64.93, Trail Blazer on Lighter).
- **venues/lighter_client.py — live-path fix**: `SignerClient.__init__` builds an aiohttp `ApiClient` internally (→ `asyncio.get_running_loop()`), so constructing it in the synchronous `LighterClient.__init__` crashed the LIVE/testnet path with `RuntimeError: no running event loop` (never hit before because the signer path can't be tested without a key). Now the signer is constructed ON the client's loop thread via `run_coroutine_threadsafe`, same as the read-only ApiClient in `_build()`. Verified with a dummy key: construction now reaches auth (fails cleanly on key validation, not the loop). Shadow/paper paths unaffected.

behaviour. **Multiple Claude sessions work this repo in parallel** — this file is
how they stay in sync. If your diff touches bot code (`*.py`, `*.sh`, a strategy,

it). Newest first. Keep entries one line; link the commit if useful.

## 2026-07-05 (later)
- ⚡ Range Raider (`DayTraderV5Gated`): DIAGNOSED the "no trades since rework" — not a bug (logs show a clean load, no populate_indicators error); it was OVER-GATED: every mode needed a pullback AND an uptrend on the same 1h candle, a rare confluence, so it sat idle in this choppy market. FIX = two new regime-covering legs so it operates regularly: `trend_breakout` (ADX≥25 + close>EMA50 + break of 20-bar high — trades RISING phases; grounded in V7's Donchian edge; `confirm_trade_exit` vetoes the range-top sell so breakouts run) and `range_meanrev` (ADX<20 chop + buy the range low, no uptrend requirement — the engine for a choppy market; low-ADX gate is the research-backed guard against knife-catching). Both fee-band gated; range_meanrev half-stake + 2.0×ATR stop. Distinct tags so the brain measures each.
